item.title: Houston's O'Shaquie Foster drops Emanuel Navarrete twice, takes his belts at 130 pounds
item.description: O'Shaquie Foster knocks down Emanuel Navarrete. Emanuel Navarrete and Texas native O'Shaquie Foster meet for the IBF, WBC and WBO world super featherweight titles on Saturday, Oct. 24,2026 at Frost Bank Center (Ronald Cortes) Emmanuel Navarrete entered the ring Saturday night as the boxer with the reputation of being a power puncher who finishes fights. However, it was O'Shaquie Foster, who grew up in Orange and lives and trains in Houston , standing over a thoroughly beaten Navarrete after a pair of 12th round knockdowns at San Antonio's Frost Bank Center on his way to a unanimous 118-108, 118-108, 115-111 decision to hold on to his World Boxing Council junior lightweight title, while taking Navarrete's World Boxing Organization and International Boxing Federation belts. "I told y'all before, I'm the better inside fighter and the better outside fighter and I feel like I proved that tonight," Foster said in the ring immediately after the win. "Hats off to him, but I knew I was levels above him and I just wanted to prove it." The 31-year-old Navarrete (40-3-1, 33 KOs) came out aggressively and the two fighters battled pretty evenly for the first four rounds, but Foster (26-3, 12 KOs) began to take control in the fifth round with effective counter punching and a sharpshooting right hand. "In this sport, it's about styles," Navarrete said. "His style was better than mine tonight." The hard-hitting Navarrete landed some power shots throughout the fight, including a right uppercut to the chin in the final 10 seconds of the 11th round that seemed to hurt Foster, but the champion held firm. "Hell yeah, he can punch, but I've got a chin," Foster admitted. "I'm strong." Although trying to determine how judges saw a fight always can be risky, it seemed pretty clear that Foster was ahead on the scorecards entering the 12th, but he was the one who chose to come out aggressively for the final round. Navarrete, who entered the night having tasted the canvas just once in his career, went down twice in the 12th. "My coaches just told me, 'Go out and put him on his ass' and that's what I did," Foster said. The first knockdown came with an overhand right, then he got him again with a right hook to the chin. "I felt like was breaking him down throughout the fight and I just timed him good in that last round," Foster said. With Foster holding three belts at 130 pounds now, he needs just to grab the World Boxing Association strap to become the first junior lightweight to unify the division since it expanded to four belts. Anthony Cacace defends his WBA belt against Nick Ball in December. "I'm trying to go undisputed for sure, so the winner out of Cacace and Ball, come see me," Foster said. Foster has long talked about getting a shot at unbeaten Shakur Stevenson, who jumped in the ring after Foster beat Raymond Ford at University of Houston's Fertitta Center and seemed to agree to fight his former training partner turned rival. item.title: Veekee James’ Sheer Beaded Bodice Leads Wine-Red Fashion at Zlatan Ibile’s Wedding | See Photos
item.description: Veekee James showcasing her custom wine-red corset dress and gold woven box clutch. Veekee James at a party? Trust her to come dressed like the celebration has its own red carpet. And when it’s a Nigerian wedding, with good music, beautiful traditional outfits and guests who take their fashion very seriously, you already know she’s going to have some fun with her look. Yesterday, Afrobeats star Zlatan Ibile , whose real name is Omoniyi Temidayo Raphael , and his partner, Davita Omoniyi , celebrated their traditional wedding with family, friends and some familiar faces from the entertainment industry. Among the guests was Nigerian fashion designer Veekee James, who arrived in a gorgeous wine-red and champagne creation from her own fashion label. And between the sculpted corset, the beaded sleeves and that towering gele, there was so much to admire. Veekee James in a custom wine-red sheer corset dress with metallic sequin detailing and a structured metallic gele. Let’s start with the dress. Veekee chose a floor-length, figure-hugging design featuring a sheer corset-style bodice covered in vertical rows of wine-red crystals. The sweetheart-inspired neckline extended into a high, embellished collar, while the long sheer sleeves featured rows of burgundy beads. The fitted skirt followed a mermaid silhouette, with sweeping patterns of gold sequins, wine-red embroidery and dusty-rose detailing running down to a subtle train. Structural details of the sheer corset bodice, crystal neckband, and sequin wave skirt on Veekee James’ wedding guest dress. And that gele! Veekee went for a tall, fan-pleated design in metallic champagne, giving her look even more height and making the headwrap a fashion moment of its own. She paired it with burgundy drop earrings, a structured gold woven box clutch and soft, neutral makeup that complemented the colours of her outfit. Styling details of Veekee James’ high-neck crystal collar, sheer corset bodice, and pleated metallic gele. Of course, Veekee knows her way around a corset. As the founder and creative director of her eponymous fashion label, she’s known for sculpted silhouettes, detailed beadwork and glamorous occasionwear. For Zlatan and Davita’s wedding, she brought those design elements into her own wardrobe, pairing a fitted, heavily embellished dress with a traditional gele. What we particularly love is how the colours work together. The deep wine-red gives the dress its richness, while the champagne and gold details brighten the overall look. Even with the crystals, beading and high neckline, the accessories have their place, from the matching earrings to the gold clutch. Veekee James posing alongside her husband Femi Atere at Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi’s wedding. And if you’ve been looking for wedding guest inspiration, Veekee’s outfit offers a lovely styling idea: when your dress has this much detail around the neckline, you can leave out the necklace and let your earrings and gele do their thing. item.title: Man United consider Bundesliga solution after major investment in attack and midfield
item.description: Man United consider Bundesliga solution after major investment in attack and midfield Manchester United are reportedly prioritising a move for RB Leipzig defender David Raum as Michael Carrick looks to strengthen his defensive options ahead of the January transfer window. According to a report from CaughtOffside , the Germany international has become a top target for the Red Devils, who are preparing to address backline weaknesses after investing heavily elsewhere in the squad. David Raum could be an ideal defensive addition The 28-year-old has established himself as a reliable Bundesliga performer, combining defensive aggression with the ability to contribute effectively in attack. Manchester United are keen to improve their left-back options, and Raum could offer an experienced solution to their ongoing concerns in that position. His ability to deliver dangerous crosses, support attacking transitions and contribute defensively would make him an attractive addition to Carrick’s squad. United have explored several alternatives, including Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde, Bournemouth’s Adrien Truffert and Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite. However, Raum is believed to be one of the more attainable options available to the Premier League giants. His contract situation could also work in United’s favour. The defender’s current agreement with Leipzig expires in the summer of 2027, which could encourage the German club to sell in January rather than risk losing him for a reduced fee later. Manchester United could secure a bargain deal for Raum Despite his importance to Leipzig, Raum could represent a financially sensible option for United compared with younger defenders commanding substantial transfer fees. The Germany international is reportedly open to testing himself in the Premier League, which could strengthen the Red Devils’ position if negotiations progress. Manchester United have already invested heavily in their attack and midfield, and defensive reinforcements are now becoming a priority. Raum’s experience and versatility could help address those concerns without requiring the club to commit an excessive fee. However, Leipzig must first decide whether they are prepared to sanction his departure midway through the campaign. With January approaching, United could accelerate their pursuit if an agreement emerges. Raum remains a promising option as Carrick looks to build a more balanced and dependable defensive unit. item.title: Stoever shuts out Steelers as Devils claim cup win
item.description: Man of the match Christian Stoever saved 31 shots for his second shutout of the season [James Assinder] Cardiff Devils took another step towards the Challenge Cup knockout stages with a tense home win against Group A leaders Sheffield Steelers. Kristoff Kontos scored the games only goal after 43 seconds of the first period, with Devils' netminder Christian Stoever making a string of outstanding saves to protect the home side's lead. The visitors also struck the pipework twice, while Cardiff's Riley Brandt and Nick Welsh went close. Despite the 1-0 final scoreline, Devils' head coach Paul Thompson described the game as a "classic win". "An absolute battle for 60 minutes, and Sheffield are a very, very good team," he said. "They probably had more offensive zone time against us than any team has had this year, but when they did get inside I thought [Stoever] was outstanding. "Sometimes you've just got to roll your sleeves up and battle, and that's what we did." With two games remaining for Cardiff they lie in third place on eight points, two behind Sheffield and Nottingham Panthers who both only have one more game to play in the group stage. Devils travel to Nottingham on Sunday, 25 October (16:00 GMT) before their final game at Manchester Storm on Sunday, 1 November. Guildford Flames, in fourth, also have 10 points with a final game at Coventry Blaze this weekend. Their hosts - and Storm - are not completely out of the running for third spot having played fewer games. The top two sides in Group A automatically qualify for the semi-final, with the third-placed team facing an elimination tie against the runners-up in the smaller group B. GB men and women to make history in Glasgow

item.title: Texas coach Steve Sarkisian calls out ticket sellers: 'They missed a hell of a game.'
item.description: AUSTIN, TX – Steve Sarkisian expressed gratitude for the Texas faithful who filled the stadium to the gills for the team’s 34-27 takedown of No. 7 Mississippi, but he also called out some apparent ticket sellers. “It was a nice night in DKR,” the Texas coach said. “For our fans, I can’t thank them enough. What an amazing atmosphere and energy DKR was again. For those fans that sold their tickets, they missed a hell of a game tonight.” If some fans sold their tickets, there was clearly a vibrant resale market, because the crowd of 104,306 exceeded the stadium’s official capacity and ranked as the fourth-largest crowd in the stadium’s history. The crowd got treated to a virtuoso performance from Texas in the first half, a furious rally from Ole Miss in the third quarter, and a game-winning touchdown run from Arch Manning on a bootleg, when he could’ve been confused for Uncle Peyton. “We’ve had that play in all season,” Manning said of his winning scoring run. He duped the Rebels with the play-fake and scored without a defender in sight. “It felt good, No one was around.” Texas overcame three turnovers and 121 penalty yards and earned another signature victory. This pelt goes alongside the September victory against Ohio State and polishes the Texas resume after it endured back-to-back SEC losses. Raleek Brown rushed for 157 yards for Texas, and the Longhorns defense made it tough on Ole Miss star quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, who threw three interceptions, including one on the game's final play. “I thought we played with Texas fight," Sarkisian said. "I thought we played with a lot of pride.” A full-house crowd saw Texas save its season. Blake Toppmeyer is the USA TODAY Network's senior national college football columnist. Listen to his podcast, " College Football Unfiltered ." Email him at BToppmeyer@gannett.com and follow him on X @btoppmeyer . item.title: Behind the scenes of a 1st NHL goal
item.description: Fans cheer for the sixth goal of the game for the Utah Mammoth as they and the Chicago Blackhawks play an NHL game at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City on Thursday, Oct. 1, 2026. | Scott G Winterton, Deseret News Both the Tampa Bay Lightning and the Utah Mammoth got to clear the bench to celebrate goals at the Delta Center Saturday night. When the game ended, though, the Mammoth were the only happy team. It was an evening to remember. Lightning superstar and reigning MVP Nikita Kucherov scored his 1,138th point to take sole possession of the franchise lead in points. That happened in the first period, so the Bolts got their bench clearing out of the way early. Bolts clear the bench to celebrate pic.twitter.com/VjFEKhFvjj — Brogan Houston (@houston_brogan) October 25, 2026 The Mammoth surmounted a 4-2 deficit to force overtime, thanks in part to Dmitri Simashev’s first NHL goal, which tied the game. Utah’s bench clearing came at the hands of Simashev a little while later, when he scored the second goal of his career — and the overtime winner. Final score: 5-4 Mammoth. “It’s fun to see um a young player like Sima come in, play the way he has all year but then get rewarded tonight with a big one,” said Utah forward Anders Lee, who also scored in the game. “Big night that I think he’ll remember for a long time.” Coincidentally, Simashev’s first two KHL goals came in similar fashion to these first two in the NHL. As was the case for him in the NHL, he went his entire first season without scoring a goal. His first one eventually came in the third period of a game, and his second came in overtime (albeit a few games later). If the past can be taken as any indication of future events, Simashev might be due for another goal soon. In the KHL, he scored his third two games after his second. Mammoth head coach André Tourigny mentioned that the game is finally starting to “slow down” for the big Russian defenseman. When coaches use that term, they mean the player feels less pressure and more confidence to make the right play. It’s a good thing. It was somewhat unexpected to see No. 26 on the ice in overtime in the first place. He has been defensively sound since he got to the NHL, but OT requires an offensive edge and Simashev hadn’t owned an NHL first-goal puck for more than an hour by the time he jumped over the boards. That’s without mentioning the fact that Utah has plenty of two-way defensemen who could have taken the assignment. Tourigny said it was defensive coach Adam Foote’s call. “Footer came to me after the the third period. You can say (we) overused some guys, and he felt Sima had legs and he was fresh, or more fresh than other guys, so he asked me, and I trust Footer’s feeling and his feel for the game, so went with that,” Tourigny said. “It was pretty good. That was a pretty good call.” Simashev thought the same thing. “I didn’t expect I’m going in overtime, to be honest. Like, thanks Footer to trust in me, and, I mean, I was just so happy when

item.title: Dodgers announcer calls for MLB to make major change after Rays' Yandy Diaz check swing controversy
item.description: Dodgers announcer calls for MLB to make major change after Rays' Yandy Diaz check swing controversy originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Entering Monday night, the Tampa Bay Rays were down one game after losing to the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 1. The Rays have refused to give up all season, and nothing less is expected of them now. Tampa Bay couldn’t have written a better start to the game. In the top of the first inning, Liam Hicks hit the first home run of the World Series to put the Rays up 4-0. “The World Series opener was all about small ball, featuring 12 singles, three stolen bases and no home runs – the first Fall Classic Game 1 without a homer since 2000. Liam Hicks muscled up and changed that narrative early, belting a two-run homer in the first inning of World Series Game 2 on Saturday evening at American Family Field that helped power the Rays’ early 4-0 lead,” MLB.com’s Bryan Hoch wrote. Those were the only runs the Rays would score on the night. The Brewers went on to win the game. “The Brewers pulled off a stunning 5-4 victory over the Rays at American Family Field, taking a 2-0 lead in their bid for the first World Series championship in franchise history. Really, at this point, there may be no stopping them. The Brewers were down 4-0 just five batters into the game, teasing the Rays that they were going to win, and then methodically came back to rip their hearts out,” USA Today’s Bob Nightengale wrote. However, the final play of the game was as controversial as it gets. Yandy Díaz checked his swing, but when the umpire was asked to appeal the call, he ruled that Díaz had swung, ending the game. After seeing the replay, World Series and Los Angeles Dodgers announcer Joe Davis called on MLB to implement a replay system for check swings, similar to the one used for balls and strikes. “We got ABS for the first time this year, getting the balls and strikes right; we need to get a system that can get [check-swings] right,” Davis said. "We got ABS for the first time this year, getting the balls and strikes right; we need to get a system that can get [check-swings] right." - Joe Davis https://t.co/PVQ1X9S4qf — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) October 25, 2026 There is no doubt that it is a heartbreaking way to lose in such a big moment. If it wasn’t a swing, the call would have kept the game alive with a walk. Díaz was frustrated, as he felt he hadn’t swung. Davis has a valid reason to call for change, as a replay system could have helped resolve the controversy surrounding the final play. Following this incident and Davis’ call for a solution, MLB could consider implementing a check-swing review system for next season. item.title: INEC Figures: How North-West, South-West may hold key to Aso Rock
item.description: •Candidates’ performance in two regions has shaped presidential election since 1999 By Luminous Jannamike Behind the battle for the presidency lies a contest over voter numbers, party machinery and political alliances. Tinubu has a head start as incumbent, but Atiku, Obi and other challengers know that no region is anybody’s political inheritance. The road to Aso Rock in 2027 runs through two regions where elections can be won, lost or thrown wide open: the North-West and South-West. Their combined electoral strength gives them enormous influence over the calculations of President Bola Tinubu and the opposition figures seeking to unseat him. The Independent National Electoral Commission’s 2026 voter register puts the North-West at 25,083,411 registered voters and the South-West at 19,614,274. Together, they account for 44,697,685 registered voters, representing more than 43 per cent of Nigeria’s 103,428,715 registered voters ahead of the 2027 general elections. Those figures make the two zones central to the presidential contest. But the real battle is more complicated than regional arithmetic. Candidates must convert registered voters into ballots, hold their traditional strongholds, penetrate rival territories and build a coalition broad enough to survive the country’s political and geographical divisions. For Tinubu, the stakes are particularly high. His South-West political base helped launch his presidential ambition, while his 2023 victory also depended on support beyond the region. Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi must find ways to disrupt that balance if they hope to deny him a second term. The numbers that can make or break a candidate The North-West’s 25.08 million registered voters make it Nigeria’s largest geopolitical voting bloc. The South-West follows with 19.61 million, ahead of the North-Central, which has 16.97 million. The political significance is unmistakable. Kano, Kaduna and Katsina are among the country’s most populous electoral states, while Lagos leads the national register with 7,488,633 voters. A candidate who makes substantial gains across these states can dramatically improve his national tally. Yet neither zone is a political inheritance. The North-West contains competing party structures, influential local leaders and voters whose choices are shaped by security, economic conditions, personalities and the performance of elected officials. Kano’s political history, in particular, shows how a powerful state-level movement can disrupt calculations made in Abuja. The South-West presents a different challenge. item.content:encoded: •Candidates’ performance in two regions has shaped presidential election since 1999 By Luminous Jannamike Behind the battle for the presidency lies a contest over voter numbers, party machinery and political alliances. Tinubu has a head start as incumbent, but Atiku, Obi and other challengers know that no region is anybody’s political inheritance. The road to Aso Rock in 2027 runs through two regions where elections can be won, lost or thrown wide open: the North-West and South-West. Their combined electoral strength gives them enormous influence over the calculations of President Bola Tinubu and the opposition figures seeking to unseat him. The Independent National Electoral Commission’s 2026 voter register puts the North-West at 25,083,411 registered voters and the South-West at 19,614,274. Together, they account for 44,697,685 registered voters, representing more than 43 per cent of Nigeria’s 103,428,715 registered voters ahead of the 2027 general elections. Those figures make the two zones central to the presidential contest. But the real battle is more complicated than regional arithmetic. Candidates must convert registered voters into ballots, hold their traditional strongholds, penetrate rival territories and build a coalition broad enough to survive the country’s political and geographical divisions. For Tinubu, the stakes are particularly high. His South-West political base helped launch his presidential ambition, while his 2023 victory also depended on support beyond the region. Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi must find ways to disrupt that balance if they hope to deny him a second term. The numbers that can make or break a candidate The North-West’s 25.08 million registered voters make it Nigeria’s largest geopolitical voting bloc. The South-West follows with 19.61 million, ahead of the North-Central, which has 16.97 million. The political significance is unmistakable. Kano, Kaduna and Katsina are among the country’s most populous electoral states, while Lagos leads the national register with 7,488,633 voters. A candidate who makes substantial gains across these states can dramatically improve his national tally. Yet neither zone is a political inheritance. The North-West contains competing party structures, influential local leaders and voters whose choices are shaped by security, economic conditions, personalities and the performance of elected officials. Kano’s political history, in particular, shows how a powerful state-level movement can disrupt calculations made in Abuja. The South-West presents a different challenge. Tinubu’s longstanding political network gives him an advantage, but it does not guarantee uniform support across the region. Lagos demonstrated this in 2023 when Obi defeated Tinubu there by 9,848 votes, polling 582,454 against the president’s 572,606. That result remains a reminder that even a candidate’s home territory can become a battleground. Party loyalty, local grievances, urban voting patterns and the credibility of candidates can all upset expectations. The numbers also require caution. INEC’s register measures people registered to vote, not the number who will eventually cast ballots. Turnout, voter accreditation, election-day logistics and the distribution of votes among candidates will determine how much of that numerical advantage translates into electoral power. What elections since 1999 reveal Nigeria’s presidential elections have repeatedly shown that regional strength matters most when it forms part of a wider national coalition. Olusegun Obasanjo’s victories in 1999 and 2003 rested on support extending beyond his South-West origins. Umaru Musa Yar’Adua’s 2007 victory reflected the strength of the Peoples Democratic Party’s national machinery, while Goodluck Jonathan’s 2011 success drew on substantial support in the South and parts of the North. The 2015 election changed the political landscape. Muhammadu Buhari’s victory demonstrated that an opposition alliance could defeat an incumbent when it combined a formidable northern base with support in other parts of the country. The merger that produced the All Progressives Congress brought together political interests that had previously competed against one another. Buhari’s re-election in 2019 again showed the importance of maintaining a broad electoral coalition, even as the contest exposed persistent regional divisions. Tinubu’s 2023 victory followed another complex pattern. He won the presidency with 8,794,726 votes, ahead of Atiku’s 6,984,520 and Obi’s 6,101,533. The result was not the product of one region alone. It reflected a combination of Tinubu’s South-West support, votes from the North and the fragmentation of opposition support across several candidates. The lesson for 2027 is not that a candidate must reproduce one previous election formula. It is that regional dominance, without alliances and sufficient support elsewhere, can leave a candidate short of victory. The 2023 result that changed the game The last election exposed the risks of treating Nigeria’s regions as predictable voting blocs. Tinubu secured 2,542,979 votes in the South-West and 2,652,235 in the North-West, according to zonal breakdown. The figures showed that his northern performance was at least as important as his home-region strength. But the North-West did not vote as a single political unit. Atiku won Kaduna with 554,360 votes against Tinubu’s 399,293, while Rabiu Kwankwaso carried Kano for the New Nigeria Peoples Party. The split deprived the opposition of a unified northern vote while also limiting Tinubu’s ability to sweep the region. In the South-West, Obi’s narrow victory in Lagos demonstrated that Tinubu’s political base could be challenged. Obi’s strength in the South-East, meanwhile, did not translate into enough votes across the country to secure the presidency. Atiku’s support in parts of the North also proved insufficient. The distribution of votes made the difference. Had opposition support been concentrated behind a single candidate, the contest could have looked very different. Instead, three major contenders divided the electorate, while Tinubu assembled enough votes across several regions to finish first. Simon Kolawole, veteran journalist and political analyst, captured the strategic calculation in his assessment of the 2023 presidential election result. “Tinubu did well in ‘two out of three’ – the South-West and the core North,” he surmised. Kolawole also noted that a winning candidate might need sizeable support from the North-Central or South-South, or both, in addition to strength in the South-West and core North. His point is central to the next contest: Commanding two major blocs may create a strong platform, but it does not remove the need to win elsewhere. The constitutional hurdle also remains. Under Section 134 of the Constitution, a presidential candidate must secure the highest number of votes cast and at least one-quarter of the votes in no fewer than two-thirds of the states and the Federal Capital Territory. Regional strength must therefore translate into both a national plurality and geographically distributed support. The road to Aso Rock runs through alliances Tinubu enters the race with the advantages of incumbency, an established party structure and a political network built over decades. But those advantages will be tested by the electorate’s assessment of his administration, particularly over the economy, living costs, jobs and insecurity. The North-West could become a referendum on the government’s handling of insecurity and economic hardship. In the South-West, the president will need to defend his political base against discontent and opposition efforts to make inroads in urban centres and states where local dynamics favour challengers. item.title: Bayern Munich star Harry Kane wins the Spanish version of the Ballon d’Or
item.description: Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images | Getty Images Ahead of the 2026 Ballon d’Or awarding ceremony, Bayern Munich star Harry Kane is the favorite to win the award. Interestingly, the Englishman picked up the Spanish equivalent of the Ballon d’Or by winning the “100 Marca” award presented by Spanish news outlet Marca (as captured by X account @iMiaSanMia ): 🏆 Harry Kane has won the ‘100 Marca’ award by @marca for the best player of the 25-26 season. Kane was voted by an international jury of 226 members, including journalists from MARCA, journalists from many other media outlets in Spain and around the world, former footballers, and coaches. Top 10: 1- Kane (3,962 points) 2- Yamal (3,937) 3- Mbappé (3,440) 4- Rodri 5- Kvaratskhelia 6- Messi 7- Fabián Ruiz 8- Olise 9- Dembélé 10- Cubarsí Kane succeeds previous winners Karim Benzema (21-22), Erling Haaland (22-23), Vinicius Jr (23-24) and Lamine Yamal (24-25). Here’s a video of Kane reacting to winning 100 Marca: Harry Kane's message after winning the '100 Marca' award for the best player of 2025/26 🏆 pic.twitter.com/glPOnP30zm — Bayern & Germany (@iMiaSanMia) October 23, 2026 This award is like the Ballon d’Or in many ways: the voting and point-scoring systems, the evaluation period (the full 2025/26 season), and, to an extent, the number of nominees. As the name suggests, Kane emerged as the best player out of 100 players on Marca’s shortlist, compared to the Ballon d’Or, which lists 30 players. Interestingly, Kane finishing in first place meant he beat fellow Ballon d’Or contenders Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappé, who finished second and third behind the Englishman in a poll where a good chunk of the panel is made up of journalists across Spain. Could we see the same rankings on Monday? Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: New, improved notifications system! item.title: Travis Kelce gets major injury update as NFL makes controversial Daiyan Henley decision
item.description: Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images Travis Kelce has received a positive injury update ahead of the Kansas City Chiefs’ meeting with the Seattle Seahawks, despite the NFL deciding against punishing Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley for the tackle that injured him. Kelce suffered an ankle injury during the Chiefs’ victory over the Chargers after a tackle that sparked questions about whether Henley had committed a hip-drop tackle. The NFL has since issued its disciplinary decisions for the relevant round of games, but Henley escaped a fine while another Chargers player was punished. Travis Kelce cleared to face Seattle Seahawks as Daiyan Henley avoids NFL punishment The Chiefs listed Kelce as a limited participant throughout the week because of his ankle problem. However, he entered the weekend without an injury designation, indicating he is available for the Seahawks matchup. Kelce initially went down in the opening quarter against the Chargers after what appeared to be a hip-drop tackle. Despite the injury, he returned to the game after the Chiefs’ medical staff taped his ankle. The veteran tight end finished with four catches for 53 yards as Kansas City secured a 22-6 victory. However, the NFL’s Office of Gameday Accountability did not include Henley among the players fined for on-field misconduct. The decision could frustrate Chiefs supporters who believed the tackle warranted disciplinary action. PJ Green of the Kansas City Star had described the incident on X, writing : “Daiyan Henley’s tackle on Travis Kelce was a sliding hip drop where his shoulder dinged Kelce’s ankle.” While Henley avoided punishment, Chargers rookie offensive guard Alex Harkey was fined $5,277 for a late hit against Kansas City early in the fourth quarter. Kelce’s availability is welcome news for the Chiefs as they look to maintain their unbeaten start to the season. A victory over the defending champion Seahawks would take Kansas City to 6-0 and keep them at the top of the AFC standings. With Patrick Mahomes and Kelce available, the Chiefs have received a timely boost ahead of a challenging road test. The focus now shifts to whether they can extend their winning run against Seattle. item.title: Texas football fans react to Longhorns' win over Ole Miss: 'A win when we needed it most'
item.description: Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning runs into the end zone untouched for a fourth quarter touchdown against Mississippi at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin on Saturday Oct. 24, 2026. (Jay Janner/Austin American-Statesman) After losing two straight games, the Texas Longhorns needed to pull off the upset over visiting Ole Miss to keep College Football Playoffs alive. And No. 19 Texas did just that with a 34-27 win over the No. 7 Rebels that came down to the wire. A pair of Longhorns (5-2, 2-2 SEC) failed to recover an onside kick and Ole Miss (5-2, 3-2) couldn't find the end zone. The Longhorns relied on its rushing attack and quarterback Arch Manning scored his first rushing touchdowns of the season while running back Raleek Brown finished the night with 157 yards. After being the subject of conversation over the last few weeks, Texas' special teams blocked a go-ahead field goal in the fourth quarter. item.title: “Very important day”: Fabrizio Romano details United players’ true feelings on Carrick ahead of Bournemouth clash
item.description: “Very important day”: Fabrizio Romano details United players’ true feelings on Carrick ahead of Bournemouth clash Manchester United suffered one of their most embarrassing European outings in Italy on Wednesday, enduring a 4-1 defeat to Champions League debutants Como. That result extended United’s winless run to seven games, and yet, it was not enough for INEOS to pull the trigger on their second failed appointment after Ruben Amorim. However, Bruno Fernandes’ post-match interview suggested the cracks are widening at Carrington and Carrick is on borrowed time. What Manchester United players think of Michael Carrick Now, Fabrizio Romano has shed some light on the atmosphere behind the scenes at United ahead of a potentially season-defining clash against Bournemouth at Old Trafford. Speaking on his YouTube channel, the Italian journalist underlined, “It’s Sunday and it’s an important day for Manchester United, a very important day for Manchester United.” It is understood United decided to give Michael Carrick more time after the Como game in order to “evaluate the situation from now to the international break. That’s why Carrick went to the media on Friday.” Carrick insisted he completely trusts the team, but Romano claims “there are some issues with the players.” The United legend is thought to be “considered by everyone at Manchester United, players, board, directors, everyone, as a fantastic person. So he has respect from everyone. It’s not about the personal relationship. Sometimes it’s about tactics, sometimes it’s about decisions. There are some players that were not happy. That’s very clear after the Como game.” Talks over potentially replacing Carrick started Romano added that United have already held internal discussions to understand “what could be the direction for a new manager if they decide to part ways with Michael Carrick.” There may be some tension at board level at the club as well, with different figures favouring different names to potentially replace Carrick. “The German part” of the United hierarchy, presumably Christopher Vivell, admire Julian Nagelsmann and Fabian Hürzeler, while some prefer Eddie Howe. Director of football, Jason Wilcox, in particular, wants someone with Premier League experience to take over the helm. Featured image George Wood via Getty Images online polls

item.title: Roberto De Zerbi hails Mateus Fernandes' elite mentality as Tottenham break Stamford Bridge curse
item.description: Chelsea FC v Tottenham Hotspur - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi was full of praise for his squad’s psychological shift following a dominant display in west London. The Italian tactician highlighted the performance of Mateus Fernandes, who remained composed throughout a high-tension London derby that saw tempers boil over in the second half. Fernandes shines in rare Bridge triumph Tottenham produced a tactical masterclass to secure a rare 2-0 victory against Chelsea , marking only their second Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in 36 years. They took full advantage of a disciplined performance and a moment of madness from Cole Palmer to silence the home crowd. De Zerbi commended his squad's fighting spirit on the pitch, singling out Fernandes for delivering 90 minutes of exceptional quality. "I love watching my players fighting on the pitch. Fernandes played 90 minutes with a big quality. I want to see him with personality, enjoying with the ball, can make a mistake, it doesn’t matter. I want to see this personality from my team. We are a big club. In the last period the results have been not so good, but we are a top club. We must show personality. We must show mentality," De Zerbi said. Youthful energy fuels Tottenham resurgence With a one-man advantage, Tottenham doubled their lead through a stunning solo effort from Mathys Tel, who cut inside from the left wing to fire past Penders. The goal capped an impressive individual performance and highlighted the growing influence of the club’s younger stars. De Zerbi noted that the development of these prospects is central to his long-term vision for the team. "Changing the spirit of the group, changing the performance of the players, especially the more fragile players, maybe the younger players. Mateus Fernandes maybe was one of the best players on the pitch, like Mathys Tel. Archie Gray is younger, but he’s older as a mentality. I’m very, very happy. We want to improve, improve, improve, to be better game by game, week by week. We have suffered enough," he remarked. Stamford Bridge hoodoo finally broken Spurs arrived at Stamford Bridge with a dismal record, having won only once at the stadium since 1990—a 3-1 victory back in 2018. However, De Zerbi was adamant that his current group should not be burdened by the failures of their predecessors. He insisted that the focus remains entirely on the future and establishing a new identity for the North London outfit. "It’s not our responsibility the results of the past. Winning the game, we are very happy for them, very proud for the club. But I think we are working to change the mentality of our club in the last seasons," De Zerbi explained. item.title: Fasoranti’s Death: Why reconciliation in Afenifere will be difficult — Okurounmu, ex-Secretary
item.description: •Group’s future uncertain —Mogaji Adejumo By Dapo Akinrefon Tongues across the country are wagging over a possible leadership crisis within the once formidable pan-Yoruba socio-political organisation, Afenifere, especially with the demise of its leader, Pa Reuben Fasoranti . Fasoranti died on Tuesday at the age of 100 years. Before his death, the Yoruba group had been engulfed in leadership crisis. It is instructive to note that Afenifere hinges on a traditional, non-competitive succession process to choose its next leader. However, the body faces the critical task of unifying its historically fractured factions. While the old guards like Chief Olu Falae express hope that a new leader will emerge seamlessly through ancestral custom, key insiders paint a much bleaker picture of the group’s future. How division set in In 2023, its then Acting Leader, late Pa Ayo Adebanjo, rocked the boat by suspending two of its officials, the National Publicity Secretary, Jare Ajayi and National Organising Committee, Abagun Kole Omololu. The suspension, however, led to a split and worsened the crisis. Both officials were removed from office and subsequently suspended for alleged uncouth activities and issuance of unauthorised statements, as well as constant denigration of the organisation. Recall that in November 2022, the late Afenifere leader, Pa Fasoranti, insisted that he remained the leader of the group. This was after he had named his deputy, late Pa Ayo Adebanjo, as the leader of the organization. Pa Adebanjo, who was taken aback over Fasoranti’s suddenly change of mind, had alleged that there was an attempt to split the organisation. Observers of events in the polity were of the view that he was not far from the truth. The split, however became a reality. It was as a result of the fact that during the 2023 electioneering campaign, then candidate of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Asiwaju Bola Tinubu had visited Pa Fasoranti in Akure, where the former Lagos State governor was endorsed. The decision did not sit well with the Adebanjo group. How Fasoranti stepped down in 2021 It will be recalled that in March 2021, Pa Fasoranti stepped down as Afenifere leader, citing old age. While Adebanjo had endorsed Peter Obi, who was presidential candidate of the Labour Party, LP, the Fasoranti group, threw its weight behind Tinubu. Fasoranti had named the deputy leader, Chief Ayo Adebanjo, as the acting national leader of the group, while the former financial secretary, Oba Oladipo Olaitan, the Alaago of Kajola Ago in Atakumosa East Council Area, Ilesa, Osun State, was named the group’s deputy leader. Fasoranti had said: “The development became necessary as the group needs, more than ever before, to have an improved organisation with a more effective approach to combat the monstrous invasion of our culture and pride as a people. “Only a more alike and active leadership can achieve this. At 95 I am hardly able to provide such and so it is time for me to step aside.

Fasoranti died on Tuesday at the age of 100 years. Before his death, the Yoruba group had been engulfed in leadership crisis. It is instructive to note that Afenifere hinges on a traditional, non-competitive succession process to choose its next leader. However, the body faces the critical task of unifying its historically fractured factions. While the old guards like Chief Olu Falae express hope that a new leader will emerge seamlessly through ancestral custom, key insiders paint a much bleaker picture of the group’s future. How division set in In 2023, its then Acting Leader, late Pa Ayo Adebanjo, rocked the boat by suspending two of its officials, the National Publicity Secretary, Jare Ajayi and National Organising Committee, Abagun Kole Omololu. The suspension, however, led to a split and worsened the crisis. Both officials were removed from office and subsequently suspended for alleged uncouth activities and issuance of unauthorised statements, as well as constant denigration of the organisation. Recall that in November 2022, the late Afenifere leader, Pa Fasoranti, insisted that he remained the leader of the group. This was after he had named his deputy, late Pa Ayo Adebanjo, as the leader of the organization. Pa Adebanjo, who was taken aback over Fasoranti’s suddenly change of mind, had alleged that there was an attempt to split the organisation. Observers of events in the polity were of the view that he was not far from the truth. The split, however became a reality. It was as a result of the fact that during the 2023 electioneering campaign, then candidate of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Asiwaju Bola Tinubu had visited Pa Fasoranti in Akure, where the former Lagos State governor was endorsed. The decision did not sit well with the Adebanjo group. How Fasoranti stepped down in 2021 It will be recalled that in March 2021, Pa Fasoranti stepped down as Afenifere leader, citing old age. While Adebanjo had endorsed Peter Obi, who was presidential candidate of the Labour Party, LP, the Fasoranti group, threw its weight behind Tinubu. Fasoranti had named the deputy leader, Chief Ayo Adebanjo, as the acting national leader of the group, while the former financial secretary, Oba Oladipo Olaitan, the Alaago of Kajola Ago in Atakumosa East Council Area, Ilesa, Osun State, was named the group’s deputy leader. Fasoranti had said: “The development became necessary as the group needs, more than ever before, to have an improved organisation with a more effective approach to combat the monstrous invasion of our culture and pride as a people. “Only a more alike and active leadership can achieve this. At 95 I am hardly able to provide such and so it is time for me to step aside. “At this junction, I am proud to announce Chief Ayo Adebanjo, a politician of the Awolowo school of thought, as Acting leader of Afenifere and Oba Oladipo Olaitan, the Alaago of Kajola Ago in Atakumosa East Local Government Area, as the Deputy Leader.” The late Afenifere leader, in a viral video had claimed: “I am still the leader of Afenifere. Afenifere has not endorsed Obi, we are endorsing Jagaban (Bola Tinubu) for the presidency. “You can see the trend, the approval and the acceptability. You could see what happened when Tinubu came to meet me in Akure. The media carried the whole thing. “Adebanjo cannot warn me not to welcome Tinubu. Can he do that successfully? “What happened was that Adebanjo took a stand and I took a stand. I didn’t call him and he didn’t call me. We never spoke about the visit. “As you can see, Jagaban is accepted and we approve of him. Obi has no stand in our mind at all.” Adebanjo counters Fasoranti But in a swift reaction, Ayo Adebanjo, known to be a staunch Awoist, faulted Tinubu’s visit to Pa Fasoranti, saying the comments trailing it were aimed at dividing the group. Adebanjo, who earlier endorsed Peter Obi, said: “Nothing is going on other than an attempt to split Afenifere to which I will not be a party. “It is a sort of conspiracy among those who want to see Afenifere divided. They have been on this plan for over a month ago and my members came to me to alert me about it and I said, ‘Don’t talk about it. It would be a diversion. All we want now is an election on issues.” He said Pa Fasoranti had called to inform him about Tinubu’s planned visit adding that the former Afenifere leader was initially not open to receiving the APC candidate but he persuaded him to do so. Adebanjo had said: “I will tell you the story and I won’t go further. Pa Fasoranti phoned me on Friday that Tinubu had phoned him and that he wanted to come and see him and he wanted to say no. I said no, don’t do that, you are an elder statesman. If he wanted to see you, why not? “As far as he is concerned, Obi’s endorsement is based on the principles of equity as the South-East has not produced a president since the return of democracy in 1999. Since the South-West and South-South have produced the president, he said it is the turn of the South-East. “South-South has had its own and I said it is remaining the South-East.” Adebanjo died and the once formidable Yoruba body became polarized. But with Fasoranti’s death, both camps are still laying claim to the leadership of the group. Falae speaks However, a former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, Chief Olu Falae, dismissed concerns about a possible succession struggle in Afenifere, saying the pan-Yoruba socio-political organisation has a tradition of producing leaders without contests or internal fights. Falae, who is now a monarch, rules out the possible division within the Yoruba fold. He said Afenifere was a self-perpetuating and self-regulating organisation in which leadership emerged through an established process rather than through competition for positions. “Leadership chooses itself. A new leader will emerge without any struggle. “It is obvious who the next leader will be, and I hope and pray it will be so this time,” he said. Is reconciliation a tall order? Vanguard was reliably informed that before Fasoranti’s death, there was underground moves to bring all Afenifere member under one roof. For instance, it Chief Sola Ebiseni, who was the General Secretary of the Adebanjo camp, had crossed over the Fasoranti camp. A senior Afenifere leader had confided in Vanguard that the reconciliation was to be unveiled immediately after the 2027 general elections. However, with Fasoranti’s demise, this may be turn out to be difficult to achieve. ‘No light at the end of tunnel’ Providing his perspective on the crisis and possible reconciliation, a former National Secretary of the Yoruba body, Senator Femi Okurounmu, said he does not see light at the end of the tunnel as far as reconciliation in Afenifere is concerned. Okurounmu, a former Senator from 1999-2003, said though it was too early to talk or reuniting the group, the two factions cannot be reconciled. In a chat with Vanguard, the former lawmaker said: “You see, it is difficult. Things are difficult. It is very difficult to unite the two groups. The Akure group supports Tinubu. You cannot criticise Tinubu in the presence of the Akure group.” Speaking further, he said: “Everything Tinubu does must be supported. That is the philosophy of the Akure group. “The Adebanjo group is very critical of Tinubu. That is an irreconcilable difference, and that is why the two groups cannot be reconciled.” Origin of crisis – Adejumo Giving his perspective on the crisis in Afenifere, Mogaji Gboyega Adejumo, a former Public Relations Officer of the body, traces the origin of the crisis. Adejumo, who is also the Gbonka Aare-Ona Kakanfo, said Afenifer

item.title: Prairie View A&M uses big run to take control, beat East Texas A&M
item.description: A run of 24 consecutive points helped Prairie View A&M take control en route to a nonconference win over East Texas A&M. (Yi-Chin Lee, Houston Chronicle / Staff photographer) COMMERCE - Prairie View A&M made it consecutive wins, beating East Texas A&M 30-19 on Saturday night at Memorial Stadium. The Panthers (4-5) took control of the nonconference game against the Lions (2-6) of the Southland Conference by scoring 24 consecutive points after trailing 6-0. Tevin Carter threw for 237 yards and two touchdowns to Rodny Ojo while Chase Bingmon ran for 77 yards on nine carries, including two TDs, for Prairie View. Bingmon's 2-yard TD run early in the second quarter put the Panthers up for good. Carter and Ojo then connected for TDs sandwiched around an Ehtan Eddins field goal to put the Panthers up 24-6 early in the fourth quarter. The Lions drew within 24-19 with 9:39 left but Bingmon's 52-yard TD run just 52 seconds later iced the Panthers' win. Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. This article originally published at Prairie View A&M uses big run to take control, beat East Texas A&M .

item.title: Maple Leafs Expose Real Oilers in Blowout Win
item.description: The Toronto Maple Leafs' blowout win on Saturday night at Rogers Place showed what the real Edmonton Oilers look like. Getty The Toronto Maple Leafs exposed the real Edmonton Oilers in a 7-2 blowout win at Rogers Place on Saturday night. Edmonton, with Connor McDavid’s insane point streak, has dominated their opponents this season. Well, that was not the case against Toronto. The Leafs opened up a 5-1 lead in the third period, capitalizing on just about every mistake the Oilers made on the night. But it wasn’t so much a question of taking advantage of mistakes. It was about shutting down the powerful Edmonton offense. Yes, Leon Draisaitl had two goals. Connor McDavid added two assists. But they were nearly as influential as they’ve been in other games. Plus, one of those patented desperate third-period comebacks that Edmonton has pulled off so many times did not come to fruition. The bottom line is that the Maple Leafs showed everyone that the Oilers have a fatal flaw, one that has followed them around for years: They don’t play defense. Auston Matthews’ tally was possible thanks to Easton Cowan making Ryan Shea look sick on the pass. MATTHEWS SNIPES IT AFTER A BEAUTY FEED FROM EASTON COWAN! pic.twitter.com/9Z0ZSmGBsp — Maple Leafs Hotstove (@LeafsNews) October 25, 2026 As for the goaltending, well, that wasn’t any better. Tristan Jarry gave up six on the night, including this headscratcher: Toronto goal! Scored by Zack MacEwen with 06:21 left in the 3rd. Assisted by Brandon Duhaime. EDM: 1 | TOR: 5 #TORvsEDM #LetsGoOilers #PassionNeverSleeps pic.twitter.com/rqfhPH0fMG — NHL Goals (@nhl_goal_bot) October 25, 2026 The Maple Leafs showed on Saturday night that when the Oilers can’t outscore their opponents, they fold like a lawn chair. Toronto deserved to win. They were better in every facet of the game. Oilers too many passengers. Didn’t match Maple Leafs competitiveness tonight. — Jason Gregor (@JasonGregor) October 25, 2026 Maple Leafs Beat Oilers at Their Own Game The entire Oilers’ game plan hinges on puck possession and control. They use speed and transitions to move the puck up ice, often catching opponents flat-footed. When looking at many of McDavid’s goals, they start with a strong rush and someone crashing the net. Leon Draisaitl’s first of the night, scored while 4-on-4, was a good example of how they controlled the entire play, eventually leading to the tally. Edmonton goal! Scored by Leon Draisaitl with 00:56 left in the 2nd. Assisted by Connor McDavid and Evan Bouchard. EDM: 1 | TOR: 3 #TORvsEDM #LetsGoOilers #PassionNeverSleeps pic.twitter.com/kEeWvR1h4r — NHL Goals (@nhl_goal_bot) October 25, 2026 The goal momentarily swung momentum in Edmonton’s favor. But it was the Maple Leafs’ strong start to the third period, with William Nylander’s power play goal essentially putting the kibosh on any comeback hopes. The bottom line is that the Maple Leafs showed everyone that the Oilers have a fatal flaw, one that has followed them around for years: They don’t play defense. Toronto deserved to win. They were better in every facet of the game. Oilers too many passengers. Didn’t match Maple Leafs competitiveness tonight. — Jason Gregor (@JasonGregor) October 25, 2026 Maple Leafs Beat Oilers at Their Own Game The entire Oilers’ game plan hinges on puck possession and control. They use speed and transitions to move the puck up ice, often catching opponents flat-footed. When looking at many of McDavid’s goals, they start with a strong rush and someone crashing the net. Scored by Leon Draisaitl with 00:56 left in the 2nd. Assisted by Connor McDavid and Evan Bouchard. EDM: 1 | TOR: 3 #TORvsEDM #LetsGoOilers #PassionNeverSleeps pic.twitter.com/kEeWvR1h4r — NHL Goals (@nhl_goal_bot) October 25, 2026 The goal momentarily swung momentum in Edmonton’s favor. But it was the Maple Leafs’ strong start to the third period, with William Nylander’s power play goal essentially putting the kibosh on any comeback hopes. Toronto Played Best Game of the Season When the final buzzer sounded, the Maple Leafs had indeed played their best game of the season. The Buds managed to mitigate the damage by Draisaitl and McDavid, while exposing the weak defense and goaltending that has characterized the Edmonton Oilers for eons now. The Leafs were coming off a concerning, if entertaining win against the New York Rangers . But if there were any concerns about Toronto, their win on Saturday went a long way to quelling them. In fact, the pounding in Edmonton reinforces the 6-3 win against the Colorado Avalanche earlier this season. Even with multiple losses on the blue line, the Maple Leafs look like a solid defensive team, with offensive contributions coming up and down the lineup. The goals by MacEwan, Troy Stecher, and Vinni Lettieri underscore just how dangerously balanced Toronto is looking this season. Oh, and let’s not forget that Anthony Stolarz had a fantastic game. Stolarz stopped 30 of 32, doing his part to stifle Edmonton’s offense. The win also moved the Leafs into the top three in the Eastern Conference. Sure, it’s still early, but the rest of the Atlantic Division has to be on notice. item.title: Mitch Johnson admits what the Spurs must continue to do to maintain their winning form
item.description: Mitch Johnson admits what the Spurs must continue to do to maintain their winning form originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Antonio Spurs have finally ended their winless run to start the 2026-27 NBA season. They lost their first two games of the year, but they finally got a win on the board by beating the Dallas Mavericks on Saturday in a 122-106 victory. It was a much better effort from the Spurs compared to what they did against the Oklahoma City Thunder and the Houston Rockets . This was a well-rounded performance that head coach Mitch Johnson appreciates and would love to continue seeing moving forward. Mitch Johnson wants to keep seeing the Spurs fighting The Spurs have one of the most talented rosters in the NBA today, but they had a slow start to the season. Everyone knows that they are contenders now, so they have to meet sky-high expectations. However, they were quite disappointing in those first two games. Victor Wembanyama, in particular, had some bad performances. Since he is considered by a large chunk of the NBA community to be a favorite to get the MVP award, the win against the Mavericks was a return to form for the 7'5" behemoth. MORE: Dylan Harper believes the Spurs fans should calm down after a slow start to the 2026-27 season Johnson also wanted to highlight something that the Spurs did against the Mavericks that was absent in the first two games. That was the effort they put into the game with hustling for the ball, rebounding, defending, and many more. That was a big deal for Johnson, and he would prefer to keep that going. "Effort goes a long way. It's as simple as it sounds. As talented as these guys are, consistent effort with just a little bit of togetherness and execution can really be something to grow upon and build upon... We just have not been consistent enough in a lot of ways," Johnson said after the Spurs' win against the Mavericks . Johnson is ready to jumpstart the Spurs' campaign now with what he has seen. In preseason, Johnson said that the Spurs weren't ready just yet, but with the performnace against the Mavs, it seems that he unlocked something that will spell trouble for the rest of the league. item.description: New York Knicks forward Jeremy Sochan (20) attends practice during the NBA finals media day at Frost Bank Center. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Daniel Benjamin, Editor Jeremy Sochan has found a new home. Sochan was selected with the No. 1 pick in the 2026 G-League Draft by the Texas Legends earlier today. The Legends, the G-League affiliate of the Dallas Mavericks , are the 2022 Top 10 draft pick’s fourth franchise over the last year. Jeremy Sochan will be the No. 1 pick of the G League Draft, sources told @hoopshype. Sochan will join the Dallas Mavericks’ affiliate, Texas Legends, and attempt to work his way back to the NBA. He’s averaged 9.9 points and 5.4 rebounds in four seasons with the Spurs and Knicks. https://t.co/Yv3cEicO3b — Michael Scotto (@MikeAScotto) October 24, 2026 Jeremy Sochan Looking For Another Chance The Portland Trail Blazers waived Sochan on October 17. Sochan, who played for the San Antonio Spurs and New York Knicks last season, signed with the Trail Blazers in early August to compete for the team’s final roster spot. But the Blazers ultimately chose to leave the spot open, Sochan played well in his limited time with Portland this preseason. The 23-year-old forward compiled 3.6 points and 2.4 rebounds in 11 minutes with shooting splits of 49.6/24.4/73.1. He scored at least six points in three of his four outings. The Spurs drafted Sochan with the 9th overall pick in the 2022 draft after one season at Baylor. The 6-8 forward was a major part of the Spurs rotation in his first season. But he saw his role reduced last season as the Spurs upgraded their talent. Sochan saw action in 28 games, though he averaged just 12 minutes a contest for the Spurs last season before being waived. A few days after being waived by the Spurs, Sochan hooked up with the Knicks, who had an open roster spot. He saw limited time with the Knicks, including 26 minutes in eight postseason appearances. Sochan is a versatile defender with a high motor capable of guarding 3-5. Sochan is a strong rebounder and secondary playmaker who excels in transition. However, he is very limited offensively in the half-court and struggles shooting from beyond the arc. However, he is very limited offensively in the half-court and struggles shooting from beyond the arc. Oklahoma City Waives Otega Oweh The Oklahoma City Thunder have released Otega Oweh from his two-way contract as he suffered a season-ending Achilles injury during the preseason. The Oklahoma City Thunder has waived guard Otega Oweh per Thunder PR — Andrew Schlecht (@AndrewKSchlecht) October 24, 2026 Oweh was selected with the No. 41 pick in this year’s draft and signed a two-way deal with the Thunder a few days after the draft. The Thunder acquired the 23-year-old on day two of the draft from Miami for Ryan Conwell, the No. 37 pick. Oweh struggled shooting the ball during the Summer League. However, Oweh appeared in all four exhibition games and showed some of his all-around ability, posting a double-double against Atlanta. He averaged 6.8 points on 40% shooting from the field and 5.0 rebounds in 24 minutes over four games before suffering an Achilles injury against the Pacers. The Thunder replace Otega Oweh with Micah Peavy Oklahoma City Thunder guard Otega Oweh (13) dribbles against Atlanta Hawks guard Nickeil Alexander-Walker (7) during the third quarter at State Farm Arena. Photo Credit: Jordan Godfree, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect The Thunder agreed to a two-way contract with Micah Peavy on Friday. So, it made sense with Oweh out for the season and his contract non-guaranteed for them to replace him. The Memphis Grizzlies waived Peavy on Monday after losing out in a competition for a spot on their final roster. The Grizzlies acquired Peavy and Jordan Hawkins from the Memphis Grizzlies for Taj Gibson and A.J. Johnson. Peavy played two preseason games with Memphis. The 25-year-old tallied 16 points on 6-of-11 shooting, five assists and two steals. He averaged 12.5 points, 3.0 assists, and 1.5 steals with 47.1/50.0/1.000/ Peavy spent all of last season with the New Orleans Pelicans after they acquired the No. 40 pick in 2025 from the Washington Wizards . While Peavy struggled to shoot, he scored in double figures 8 times in 61 games, topping 20 points twice. Peavy is a multi-positional wing defender with high motor skills. But his shooting is a big question mark. Minnesota Timberwolves guard Terrence Shannon Jr. (1) drives to the basket through New Orleans Pelicans guard Micah Peavy (14) in the second half at Target Center. Mandatory Credit: Jesse Johnson, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect The Last Word on 2022 Top 10 NBA Draft Pick Finds New Landing Spot Sochan is headed to a rebuilding Mavericks organization that is 1-2 on the season and dealing with several injuries. Kyrie Irving , Cooper Flagg , Caleb Martin, Tarik Biberovic , Santi Aldama and Dereck Lively II are the injured players. So, while Sochan has to prove he is still an NBA player with the Legends, he is in an ideal spot to get another chance, as the Mavs are projected to struggle this entire season. Unfortunately, Oweh suffered a season-ending injury, but it made sense that the Thunder felt the need to replace him, as it is a long season since his contract is non-guaranteed and doesn’t count against the cap. Peavy is a strong fit for the Thunder, as he is a defense-centric wing with upside and just the type of prospect that general manager Sam Presti likes. He joins Josh Dix and Brooks Barnhizer . item.title: Oil Spill in Delta: When environment is destroyed from within and without – black tide ‘swallows 216 communities’
item.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi The water at Odidi struggles to flow. It sits, thick, black, and dead. For seven months, the 28-inch Trans-Forcados Pipeline at the Kantu-Odidi axis, Warri South-West LGA has bled crude and associated gas into the creeks. What was sighted February 19, 2026 as a single rupture has become a black tide that has swallowed over 216 communities, according to their leaders. This is no longer just an oil spill. It is a war of narratives about who is destroying the Niger Delta — from within, or from without? On one side, the Joint Investigation Visit, JIV, of February 20-21, 2026, conducted by the National Oil Spill Detection and Response Agency, NOSDRA, officials and community representatives, gave a technical verdict: Corrosion and equipment failure. No sabotage. On the other side, voices from inside the Niger Delta say the truth is more uncomfortable. That Odidi has been a hub of illegal bunkering for 25 years and that hot-taps have turned the pipeline into Swiss cheese. Between those two truths, the environment dies. Seven months of nothing Odidi Federated Community is angry because containment has been a theatre. Comrade Justin Gbenekama, Chairman of the community, narrated: “This spill occurred on the 19th of February 2026, and up to this moment as we speak, the operator, Heritage Energy Operational Services, HEOSL, has not done anything properly to contain the spill. “As you can see within the environment, even their recovery activities is not effective.” He measured the scale of tidal spill: “And so six hours flow from this point, you get to Escravos area. And where we are standing is just five minutes drive to Forcados River, 10 minutes to the Escravos Bar. So the spill has spread very far.” For the people, the consequences are immediate. Drinking water is contaminated with hydrocarbons. Fishing and farming are dead. Cooking is a risk. Gbenekama added: “And most importantly, there is no medical attention to any of the affected communities. And even relief materials that were brought were not adequate.” He called the recovery method futile: “They will scoop, take it (spilled crude) back to their station in Isoko and inject it back to the same line, and the oil here will still come out in this point. That is an exercise in futility.” His demand: “There should be immediate shutdown of the Trans-Forcados Pipeline and carry out the complete repair before operation will commence.” It is a demand backed by law. item.content:encoded: By Egufe Yafugborhi The water at Odidi struggles to flow. It sits, thick, black, and dead. For seven months, the 28-inch Trans-Forcados Pipeline at the Kantu-Odidi axis, Warri South-West LGA has bled crude and associated gas into the creeks. What was sighted February 19, 2026 as a single rupture has become a black tide that has swallowed over 216 communities, according to their leaders. This is no longer just an oil spill. It is a war of narratives about who is destroying the Niger Delta — from within, or from without? On one side, the Joint Investigation Visit, JIV, of February 20-21, 2026, conducted by the National Oil Spill Detection and Response Agency, NOSDRA, officials and community representatives, gave a technical verdict: Corrosion and equipment failure. No sabotage. On the other side, voices from inside the Niger Delta say the truth is more uncomfortable. That Odidi has been a hub of illegal bunkering for 25 years and that hot-taps have turned the pipeline into Swiss cheese. Between those two truths, the environment dies. Seven months of nothing Odidi Federated Community is angry because containment has been a theatre. Comrade Justin Gbenekama, Chairman of the community, narrated: “This spill occurred on the 19th of February 2026, and up to this moment as we speak, the operator, Heritage Energy Operational Services, HEOSL, has not done anything properly to contain the spill. “As you can see within the environment, even their recovery activities is not effective.” He measured the scale of tidal spill: “And so six hours flow from this point, you get to Escravos area. And where we are standing is just five minutes drive to Forcados River, 10 minutes to the Escravos Bar. So the spill has spread very far.” For the people, the consequences are immediate. Drinking water is contaminated with hydrocarbons. Fishing and farming are dead. Cooking is a risk. Gbenekama added: “And most importantly, there is no medical attention to any of the affected communities. And even relief materials that were brought were not adequate.” He called the recovery method futile: “They will scoop, take it (spilled crude) back to their station in Isoko and inject it back to the same line, and the oil here will still come out in this point. That is an exercise in futility.” His demand: “There should be immediate shutdown of the Trans-Forcados Pipeline and carry out the complete repair before operation will commence.” It is a demand backed by law. Because the JIV ruled out third-party interference, HEOSL bears absolute liability under Nigerian environmental law. The operator must fund 100 percent of clean-up and compensation. And the Federal High Court in Port Harcourt, in Suit No. FHC/PH/CS/132/2026, HRM Udogri Isaac I v. Heritage Energy & NOSDRA, ordered a mandatory injunction to cease discharge and clean up all impacted ecosystems. No more business as usual Ijaw Youth Council, IYC, says it has had enough. Its President, Dr. Doubra Collins Okotete, led youths to threaten total shutdown of OML 42, OML 30 and the Forcados Terminal. “Today we are here not for jokes, but to shut down the operations of the Heritage Oil and Gas Services. This spill has been on for over seven months. The operators of Heritage are heartless, wicked,” Okotete declared. He dismissed the sabotage argument: “This is not sabotage. This is pure equipment failure. And we all know this oil activity has been going on for a very long time. “And this pipeline has been damaged for over six, seven months, yet no tangible has been done.” He alleged: “All they do is to employ contractors to come and curtail oil, yet the contractors they have employed could not contain this oil because, what as the community chairman said, they come here scoop the oil, take it back to their station, inject it back to the same Trans-Forcados Pipeline, and this oil keep popping out, destroying our ecosystem, creating health hazard for our people.” Okotete linked Odidi to the wider Niger Delta crisis, including Bille in Rivers State: “The same thing is happening to Alakiri, Rivers State, same thing that happening to Bille, Rivers State, and other communities across the Ijaw nation that are being threatened, that today life expectancy has dropped.” His message to Abuja was blunt: “President Tinubu, you are the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Federal Republic of Nigeria. The Minister, Senator Heineken Lokpobiri, this is under your watch and today our river has been bastardized.” And to the companies: “If they are tired of exploiting our oil, they should leave our environment.” Uncomfortable truth from within But long-time environmental monitor and Coordinator, Niger Delta Peace Coalition (NDPC), Zik Gbemre, offers a counter-punch that many in the creeks do not want to hear. He said Odidi’s black tide is also self-inflicted. “The Odidi axis in OML 42 has served as an active hub for illegal bunkering for over 25 years. What is happening there today is not a new development”, Gbemre said. “The ongoing environmental degradation is largely artificial and directly tied to pipeline sabotage. “Even after comprehensive cleaning and proper remediation, fresh spills reoccur within days because the root cause remains unchecked.” According to him, the pipeline is being killed by repeated hot-taps: “What is unfolding across the Odidi and Egwa fields is the direct impact of illegal bunkering operations. “Repeatedly placing hot taps on the same pipeline segments severely compromises structural integrity over time. “Even when damaged points are clamped and repaired, the weakened metal around the hot taps continues to deteriorate, making future leaks inevitable.” Gbemre, who has flown with Shell’s spill team over Odidi, said complicity is local: “A total stranger cannot enter a community, transport heavy equipment, and place hot taps on high-pressure pipelines without the knowledge, authorization, or passive approval of host community leaders and influential actors.” He listed it clearly: “Illegal bunkerers: Physical installation of hot taps, line breaching, and crude siphoning. Host Community leaders: Granting access, and providing cover.” His warning is moral: “You cannot destroy infrastructure, profit from illegal trade, and present yourself purely as an innocent victim. “You cannot demand millions in cleanup funds while harboring the very individuals who will re-break the pipes tomorrow.” He also punctured the IYC claim that surveillance by Tantita and others has ended vandalism: “It’s funny to hear the IYC boss claiming ‘no more vandalism in the operations space because TANTITA and other surveillance contractors are securing the space. “That is joke of the year and media gymnastics to justify sustenance of the multi-thrillion naira surveillance contracts. Oil theft still thrives.” Both sides in order Media consultant and Coordinator, Journalists for Just Development of the Niger Delta, Austine Aghomi, says both narratives must be held together to understand the ticking bomb. “Yes, NOSDRA is bound to do its work without bias when there are eventualities, just as oil and gas operators need to take responsibility on routine maintenance of their assets, particularly ageing pipeline from failure,” Aghomi said. He added: “What is equally concerning, however, is the realisation that unrestrained assets vandalism, particularly tapping into oil wellheads, flowlines and pipelines to steal crude oil now helps to hasten the ageing of pipelines beyond manufacturers’ set lifespan. “The lines suffer repeated cuts from oil thieves. Over time, assets operators get overwhelmed by repeated repairs and ultimately forced replacement earlier than normal.” Heritage Energy, through its Community Relations Manager Jeremiah Oharisi, told protesting women: “Heritage is more than willing to do the right thing.” But trust is gone. The pipeline is 50, its life was 25 The hard fact remains. Most trunklines in t

item.title: Ravens rule out Lamar Jackson; Tyler Huntley to start vs. Bengals
item.description: Oct 11, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Baltimore Ravens quarterback Tyler Huntley (5) celebrates with quarterback Lamar Jackson (8) after a touchdown during overtime against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Baltimore Ravens downgraded quarterback Lamar Jackson’s status from ‘questionable’ to ‘out’ ahead of their Week 7 matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals. Backup Tyler ‘Snoop’ Huntley will make his third straight start after an overtime win over the Falcons and a disappointing loss to the Browns. Jackson’s comments on Friday, as well as his limited practice participation all week, portended this outcome. He revealed that he suffered a high ankle sprain and was struggling to put weight on his left leg when running. He indicated that he did not need to be 100% to take the field, but emphasized that he would be doing a “disservice” to his team if he plays before his body is ready. Downgrading Jackson’s status is reminiscent of the lead-up to last year’s Week 8 matchup against the Bears. He suffered a hamstring injury three weeks prior and returned to practice with limited-limited-full participation days and a questionable designation on the injury report. However, Jackson did not speak to media that week, and the team only changed his status after reports emerged that he was not expected to play. This year, Jackson provided rare clarity regarding his injury, answering over a dozen questions about his status. Despite his multiple references to a “grace period” before making a decision, it was clear that he was not ready to play as of Friday. Rapid improvements in time for a Sunday afternoon kickoff were never likely. Saturday’s reports also characterized Jackson as a game-time decision. The differences from last year’s approach should ensure the Ravens avoid another league investigation that resulted in a $100,000 fine. At face value, it seems unclear why the Ravens had to update Jackson’s status on Saturday, especially if he is in that 50-50 range. Baltimore has let plenty of other players go through a pregame workout and announced their status via the inactive list 90 minutes before kickoff. It would actually benefit the team to force their opponents to prepare for Jackson to start and sit. But a two-time MVP moves betting lines, and the league is inextricably tied with sportsbooks. If Jackson is not playing, that information (from their perspective) has to be made public.
