item.title: O’Shaquie Foster Freezes Out Emanuel Navarrete Saturday
item.description: What to Know In a dominant and driven performance, O’Shaquie Foster froze out Emanuel Navarrete, becoming the unified super featherweight champion in San Antonio on Saturday Foster dropped Navarrete three times in the final round to seal his impressive victory. In the co-main event, Albert “Chop Chop” Gonzalez made his case as the 2026 Prospect of the Year. We’re believers. What to Know Three belts will be on the line in a sensational super featherweight unification fight between Emanual Navarrete and O’Shaquie Foster Saturday at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio. In the co-feature, undefeated prospect Albert “Chop Chop” Gonzalez will take on two-time world title challenger Edward Vazquez The fight card airs on DAZN Boxing with the main card at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT. Before the bell action starts at 5:30 p.m. ET/2:30 p.m. PT. on DAZN, Top Rank and DAZN’s YouTube channels, and the Top Rank Classics FAST channel on Roku, Tubi, Pluto and Vizio. O’Shaquie Foster dared to put his hand on a hot stove Saturday, but by the force of his will and skill, he put Emanuel Navarrete into a deep freeze. O’Shaquie Foster made a serious bid as the 2026 Fighter of the Year with a cool as ice performance over Emanuel Navarrete Saturday. Photo: Top Rank Boxing In nothing less than a tour de force, Foster of Orange, Texas (26-3, 12 KOs) confronted the offense of Navarrete of Mexico (40-3-1, 33 KOs) head on with a fearless determination, disarming him and eventually wearing him down. After scoring three knockdowns in the final round, not even the Texas judges could mess this one up. Two judges got it right at 118-108, with a third seeing it at 115-111. Foster wins the IBF and WBO titles from Navarrete, and the vacant Ring Magazine belt, while defending his WBC World Featherweight title. “There was no way they could rob me. I controlled every round … I knew I was doing the most work in there,” said Foster. In the co-feature, undefeated prospect Albert “Chop Chop” Gonzalez will take on two-time world title challenger Edward Vazquez The fight card airs on DAZN Boxing with the main card at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT. Before the bell action starts at 5:30 p.m. ET/2:30 p.m. PT. on DAZN, Top Rank and DAZN’s YouTube channels, and the Top Rank Classics FAST channel on Roku, Tubi, Pluto and Vizio. After scoring three knockdowns in the final round, not even the Texas judges could mess this one up. Two judges got it right at 118-108, with a third seeing it at 115-111. Foster wins the IBF and WBO titles from Navarrete, and the vacant Ring Magazine belt, while defending his WBC World Featherweight title. “There was no way they could rob me. I controlled every round … I knew I was doing the most work in there,” said Foster. SHOCK DROPS NAVARRETE IN THE FINAL ROUND! ⚡ #NavarreteFoster | Live NOW on DAZN ▪️ https://t.co/GxztAYcmYt — DAZN Boxing (@DAZNBoxing) October 25, 2026 “I worked so hard to get here, man,” said a smiling Foster. “I knew he was gonna be strong. I knew he was gonna be awkward. He’s a great champion. I just had a little bit more in me tonight,” said Foster. Navarrete was equally gracious toward the new unified champion. “What I have to say, it’s short, acceptable, and it’s professional. In this sport, it’s about styles. His style was better than mine tonight. He won tonight. Everyone, please applaud for him,” said Navarrete to his many fans in San Antonio. Foster Shows He’s More Than a Tactical Genius O’Shaquie Foster had more than enough firepower and was willing to use it to keep Emanuel Navarrete at bay. Photo: Top Rank Boxing Navarrete said he knew fans didn’t want to see a defensive fight. Given Foster’s superior technical skills, fans expected him to slow the pace and fight Navarrete at a safe distance, given his exceptional ring IQ, defense, and hand-and-foot speed. Foster and his trainer Bobby Benton must have realized he had the skills to engage with Navarrete and disarm him as the savvy ring general who is cool under fire. He stood his ground with confidence and healthy defiance, proving critics wrong in predicting he wouldn’t try to engage Navarrete in a firefight. “He’s an awkward, strong champion. Man, it was a long night. He’s got heavy hands. But I’ve got a chin, and I’m not really worried about power. I’ve got my own,” said Foster. Foster’s knockout rate is deceiving. He doesn’t always need to move in to stop the fight. But on Saturday after the 11 th round, Benton encouraged Foster to go for it. The three knockdowns didn’t end in a knockout, but they left an undeniable mark on the performance. “I felt like I was breaking him down. I wanted him to overwork, played a little mind games with him. Coming into the fight I knew I was going to be able to run him into shots, and that’s what I did.” O’Shaquie Foster scored three knockdowns in the final round to seal his victory. Photo: Top Rank Boxing Foster reflected on his accomplishment, something ten years in the making, after being incarcerated, then deciding to pursue boxing and stick with it after several early career losses. Now, Foster and trainer Bobby Benton have legitimate claims as possible 2026 Fighter and Trainer of the Year. “Words can’t even explain. It took a lot of work, a lot of sacrifice, and a lot of belief, especially where I’ve come from. “I want to go undisputed, man. My dream is to become undisputed and make history. All I need is one more to fulfill my biggest dream and then see Shakur,” said Foster. Boxing fans are already anticipating that all-American showdown. Foster’s priority is the winner of the December 19 fight in Belfast between WBA World Super Featherweight champion Anthony Cacace and former champion Nick Ball. But before any of this happens, remember that the WBO granted Navarrete the unification bout with Foster on the condition that the winner defend the WBO title against Charly Suarez of the Philippines within 180 days. Garner holds the WBC interim title, while Zaurbek won the IBF eliminator. Chop Chop Gonzalez Ready To Rumble With the Champions Albert “Chop Chop” Gonzalez made his case as 2026 Prospect of the Year. Photo: Top Rank Boxing Unbeaten featherweight Albert “Chop Chop” Gonzalez of Moreno Valley, California expected to face a test against Fort Worth native and former two-time world title challenger Edward Vazquez of Fort Worth, Texas . Ummm, things didn’t exactly work out that way. Uno, dos, adios. ALBERT CHOP CHOP GONZALEZ GETS IT DONE IN 2 ROUNDS! 😱 #NavarreteFoster | Live NOW on DAZN ▪️ https://t.co/rmk7S5Wj8k — DAZN Boxing (@DAZNBoxing) October 25, 2026 Gonzalez (19-0, 12 KOs) landed 28 power shots out of 53 landed punches in four minutes. Almost half went to the body of Vazquez of Fort Worth, Texas (20-4, 6 KOs) . Vazquez came out aggressively but landed only nine punches on Gonzalez before being dropped. Consider this: the only other opponent to stop Vazquez, featherweight world champion Rafael “Divino” Espinoza, needed seven rounds to stop Vazquez on body shots in May 2025. “I wanted to stay in the pocket a little bit, see what his pressure choices were, and when I seen he was a little slow in the pocket, I knew I could catch him in between the shots and land that body shot,” said Gonzalez. “The body’s on my mind every single fight.” Gonzalez said he was surprised when Vazquez couldn’t beat the count of referee Laurence Cole, but said it would have only delayed the same result. Gonzalez mentioned that he’d be willing to join trainer Robert Garcia in traveling to Riyadh, where WBC champion Rafael “El Divino” Espinoza’s original opponent dropped out. But Chop Chop won’t get his chance. A replacement is already scheduled. Gonzalez credited Robert Garcia and the entire RGBA team for his four-fight knockout streak . With Saturday’s win, Gonzalez jumped to the top of our 2026 Prospect of the Year list. Frank Martin Finding His Way Back Frank Martin pinned an elusive Tarik Zaina in the corner and left his left hook do the work. Photo: Top Rank Boxing Super lightweight contender Frank Martin of Indianapolis (20-1-1, 14 KOs) faced a tricky opponent and a solid game plan as he returned to the ring on Saturday. Tarik Zaina of Morocco (18-4-1, 12 KOs), who trains in Tijuana, Mexico, said Martin was the opponent he always wanted to face. In the early rounds, it was easy to see why. Zaina used his reach and movement to frustrate Martin early. The San Antonio fans began to boo, unhappy about the lack of serious action. Eventually Martin settled in, settled down, and didn’t get anxious. He figured out how to handle Zaina. It paid off with a sensational seventh-round TKO win. From ringside 😱 @TheGhost_2016 | @DAZNBoxing https://t.co/j7LxIyRovx — Top Rank Boxing (@trboxing) October 25, 2026 Martin caught Zaina with a solid left hook count

item.title: Why Pat McAfee apologised to Nick Saban for ‘ruining the whole sport’ on College Gameday
item.description: Photo by Ella Hall/LSU/University Images via Getty Images "} Pat McAfee addressed legendary coach Nick Saban when he went off about all the criticism he has received for his signature move on College GameDay. Pat McAfee has become one of the most famous sports personalities in the country in recent years. He has become one of the faces of ESPN’s College GameDay as well, alongside fellow analysts like Kirk Herbstreit and legendary college coach Nick Saban. One of McAfee’s signature moves on the show has been taking his shirt off upon urging from the crowds at the various college football games they go to. This weekend, the crew was in Salt Lake City, Utah ahead of the Utes-Cougars clash. Pat had a point to make, it would seem, and he addressed Saban while doing so. Pat McAfee called out NYT again while taking his shirt off, jokingly saying sorry for ‘ruining the sport’ McAfee’s exuberance is what makes him endearing to a lot of fans, but it is also what has earned him some detractors. His tendency to create a spectacle out of himself has been criticised by some, including the New York Times, and there are those who would prefer for the focus to stay on the game. It seems McAfee is not a fan of being called out. Because after he initially said he wouldn’t take his shirt off this time, that’s exactly what he did. He then threw a jab at NYT while talking to Saban. “New York Times already saying it,” McAfee said during College GameDay . “This a****** is shirtless at 9:02 a.m. Eastern. Sorry, Coach. I’m ruining the whole sport. I’m ruining the whole sport because of this. I just enjoy it too much not to have a good time.” McAfee is unlikely to stop doing what is clearly so popular among the crowds he performs most often in front of. His apology was obviously a dig at his critics more so than being genuine. This seems like a battle McAfee will be fighting for some time. item.content:encoded: Adri Mehmeti outshines Lionel Messi as New York Red Bulls upset Inter Miami in tight MLS playoff chase originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . HARRISON, N.J. — Fans flocked to Sports Illustrated Stadium on Saturday evening to be wowed by Lionel Messi . Instead, they were treated to the Adri Mehmeti show. The 17-year-old American kid outshined the greatest player of all-time as the New York Red Bulls overwhelmed Inter Miami 2-0 to secure a massive three points in the MLS playoff race. From the opening whistle, the Red Bulls pressed the Herons into oblivion, forcing an early own-goal off Casemiro and missing a host of other clear-cut chances created directly off turnovers. Through it all, Mehmeti was central to their ability to overwhelm the visitors in midfield. In the first 15 minutes of the match, Inter Miami held 72 percent possession, but played practically the entire time in their own half, unable to get out of jail while being overwhelmed on the ball. That continued all first half, as the visitors could not string anything cohesive together and were routinely caught out and countered. It was a team effort from the hosts, truly, but Mehmeti's influence in midfield was undeniable. "We hope it was a spectacle in the most positive sense," said Red Bulls head coach Michael Bradley after the game. "We understand the responsibility that, on certain nights, when certain teams come here with certain players, the spotlights come on a little brighter. That's our chance to show we have a pretty good team too." It was Mehmeti, not Messi, who snatched the spotlight. Having just accepted the 2026 Princess of Asturias Award for Sports out in Spain just two days prior, Messi did not start the match. As Inter Miami floundered throughout the first half and into the early part of the second half, the hugely pro-Miami crowd repeatedly chanted his name, hoping for their Argentine legend to come save the day. But even when he came on just past the hour mark, to great cheers and elation — the loudest the crowd was all evening — he was ineffective, hemmed in by the Red Bulls and left on an island with little help. That had everything to do with Mehmeti. Playing alongside Ghanan international Mohammed Sofo, who was moved from his usual No. 10 position into a dual No. 8 role alongside Mehmeti, the American youngster shined throughout the match. Mehmeti led the Red Bulls with 82 touches and 55 accurate passes in his 85 minutes, able to keep Inter Miami's possession in front of him almost the entire way through. "What else can I say?" asked Sofo of his midfield partner Mehmeti, "I mean, when you look at the quality he has, especially his age also, it's unbelievable. "Since I switched my position to No. 8, I think our connection has been amazing so far. I just hope we can play more games together. "The maturity he has is unbelievable," Sofo said. "The vision he has, he knows when to play forward, when to calm down. Sometimes he does things I'm like 'wow.' For me, as a No. 8 or also as a No. 10, I try to find myself in the pockets, and sometimes he finds me with just two touches. Other players need to take a first touch, look for it, and then play it. But for him, he can just...second touch, he finds you." It was the culmination of all of Mehmeti's best skill sets — passing, positioning, range, ball-stopping, and pressing — that came together on one evening to allow him to boss the match. Adri Mehmeti just toying with a World Cup winner in Rodrigo De Paul here 🇺🇸 Only a matter of time until Mehmeti is getting a real run with the USMNT. Just 17. https://t.co/c3wvf85kGY — Joseph Lowery (@joeclowery) October 24, 2026 "For a young player, Adri has...really good starting points," Bradley told reporters after the match. "He has personality, he has technical ability — the technical ability that you need to play in that spot when spaces are tight and things happen fast — he has a feel and understanding for the game, and the way things have gone this year, we've thrown an incredible amount at him. "I didn't know coming into the season what exactly it was going to mean for Adri," the Red Bulls' coach continued. "We knew that they [the young players] were going to be a real part of the first team, and in the end we were going to see how it played out — how they responded every day, how they took to ideas, how they pushed themselves along in a group, how they earned respect. "We have put a lot on Adri's plate. We expect a lot of him, he has a lot of responsibility in our team for a 17-year-old and he doesn't bat an eye." USMNT fans got a taste of what Mehmeti can bring to the midfield during the latest international break, but it was still just that — a taste. He played a total of 80 minutes across his first three international caps, 62 of which came in the 4-2 win over Chile. This match tonight against Messi and company was vintage Mehmeti, if such thing for a teenager exists. He dazzled on the ball, passed to every corner of the pitch, completed both his tackles, and led all outfield players in the match with 10 recoveries, tied with World Cup winner Rodrigo De Paul. By the end of the game, FotMob’s statistical algorithm had named Mehmeti as Man of the Match, while he had the second-highest individual rating on SofaScore behind the nonsensically high number for Inter Miami goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair. The win was huge for the Red Bulls, who are teetering on the cusp of the MLS playoff cut line. The three points moved them back onto solid ground — only just — as they reclaimed the ninth spot in the Eastern Conference, the final postseason position. With just three matches remaining, the race is incredibly tight. With 39 points, the Red Bulls are just one point ahead of the Columbus Crew and three clear of Toronto. Meanwhile, FC Cincinnati and Orlando City each sit on 42 points just above hem in seventh and eighth. "Obviously you knew when you win balls in dangerous spots that there's going to be space, and we were able to take that space and capitalize on it and make good chances to score the two goals," Mehmeti said after the match. "We played our football with our ideas, and the way the guys just kept on going, kept pushing through, even when they [Inter Miami] had long spells of possession, was great. So yea, it was a really good performance, and we go on to the next one." On the national team level, the star of 17-year-old sensation Cavan Sullivan has risen exponentially in recent months, and he stands to be an exciting player for the USMNT in the coming years, but Mehmeti might be the most important young player in the talent pool. He will have his work cut out for him breaking into a national team midfield that boasts the likes of Weston McKennie, Tyler Adams, Johnny Cardoso, Sebastian Berhalter, and Gio Reyna, but fans hope he can be the anchor of the next generation of midfield talent. There's a long way to go for that to happen, but on the pitch in Harrison, New Jersey tonight, he stole the show from the greatest of all-time. That, at the very least, is something to get very excited about.

item.title: 4 Lafayette area volleyball teams take home regional championships
item.description: MONTICELLO — One of the only three teams that beat No. 7 (4A) Harrison volleyball in the regular season, No. 2 Westfield, was the team the Raiders were going to have to beat to win the regional championship Saturday, Oct. 24, at Twin Lakes High School. Despite giving the Rocks a battle in the second set, the result was the same. Harrison fell in a 3-0 sweep (25-12, 25-21, 25-15), concluding a year for the program that brought its fourth consecutive sectional championship win. “Just even from last year to this season is the trust and commitment and family that they were on the court,” coach Jacklyn Lehe of the team’s growth. “I wish we could’ve fought just a little bit harder (Saturday), but I have a great group of girls.” More: Rossville volleyball stuns No 1 Covington, repeats as regional champion More: Faith Christian boys soccer's postseason run ends with crushing loss The postseason hopes ran deep for the Raiders heading into the tournament. Ending the season with 19 straight wins, they dominated most of their slate. But Westfield (27-2) presented a different challenge than most of the opponents they’ve countered, carrying size and speed across the board that was tough to match up against. Harrison has had to rely on its youth all season. It only has four seniors on the roster, three of which have been unavailable for the postseason, and 10 of its 15 players are underclassmen. But even with that inexperience, they’ve stepped up throughout the sectional run and gave the Rocks a battle in several pockets of Saturday’s loss. “We gave it our all. Every practice, every ball we had,” sophomore Gia Stokes said. “It sucks with our situation, the three seniors gone, I think the underclassmen did a really good job stepping it up and the ability for them to come off and play against a fast-paced Westfield team … is just awesome.” The outlook for the Raiders is bright with their youth, as disappointing as the end of the year was. Stokes became a team captain this season and had a team-high of 363 kills coming into the game. Freshman Story Nixon blossomed at setter with 894 assists. Stella Snider will be a leading senior for the squad and development should continue with other returners and emerging freshmen that come up. Harrison (28-4) isn’t going anywhere away from being a threat in Class 4A in 2027. “We’re losing our big middle, but we’re bringing back our outside, our center, our DSs and we have fresh middles coming in,” Lehe said. “I’m excited to keep building this program and I’m excited to see what these girls are going to do next year.” The big middle in question is Eva Stokes, a Purdue track and field commit and the player that has held down the fort in the middle over her career. But even with that inexperience, they’ve stepped up throughout the sectional run and gave the Rocks a battle in several pockets of Saturday’s loss. “We gave it our all. Every practice, every ball we had,” sophomore Gia Stokes said. “It sucks with our situation, the three seniors gone, I think the underclassmen did a really good job stepping it up and the ability for them to come off and play against a fast-paced Westfield team … is just awesome.” The outlook for the Raiders is bright with their youth, as disappointing as the end of the year was. Stokes became a team captain this season and had a team-high of 363 kills coming into the game. Freshman Story Nixon blossomed at setter with 894 assists. Stella Snider will be a leading senior for the squad and development should continue with other returners and emerging freshmen that come up. Harrison (28-4) isn’t going anywhere away from being a threat in Class 4A in 2027. “We’re losing our big middle, but we’re bringing back our outside, our center, our DSs and we have fresh middles coming in,” Lehe said. “I’m excited to keep building this program and I’m excited to see what these girls are going to do next year.” The big middle in question is Eva Stokes, a Purdue track and field commit and the player that has held down the fort in the middle over her career. She’s been with Lehe since she took the job four years ago, and watching her and the rest of the seniors grow has made that batch a special group for Lehe that’s bittersweet to see leave. In the locker room before the Raiders headed home, Stokes told her teammates to “be leaders.” Her and the rest of class may be gone, but being a leader by example is something that they hope to pass down. “We’re going to have a lot of sophomores and juniors next year,” Lehe said, “But I think they can do it because they had a great role model to show them the way.” And the players themselves believe that, too. I think they’ve foreseen it now, in the future they’re going to be good. We’re going to be able to compete with the bigger Indy teams.” West Lafayette sweeps Leo While Harrison's season ended, others around the Lafayette area extended theirs. West Lafayette (21-12) approached this week’s matchup with Leo feeling confident that they could breakthrough the regional round, and that they did. It’s their first regional championship since 2021. West Lafayette defeated Leo 3-0 (25-21, 25-22, 25-11). Between sectionals and regionals, it still has yet to drop a single set to an opponent. At the Northwood semi-state bracket, the Red Devils will take on West Noble (30-3) in the second semifinal at 12:30 p.m. Saturday, Oct. 31. A win would send them to the semi-state championship match later that night at 7 p.m. Benton Central takes down Muncie Burris In Class 2A, the Bison (24-6) went back-to-back in the regional championship, defeating Muncie Burris (24-6) in a 3-1 (23-25, 32-20, 25-23, 25-17) win. Benton Central will face Oak Hill (24-8) in the Peru semi-state bracket as it seeks to make the state championship game in Class 2A once again. That match will be at 10 a.m. Saturday, Oct. 31, with the potential title game at 6 p.m. Rossville, South Newton advance in 1A Rossville (26-7) completed a 3-2 (23-25, 17-25, 25-18, 26-24, 21-19) comeback win over the No. 1 (1A) Trojans (31-4) to go back-to-back in the regional championship. Meanwhile, South Newton won a five-set thriller over No. 4 Marquette Catholic (25-27, 25-20, 25-22, 24-26, 15-13). Both teams are on opposite sides of the 1A semi-state draw at Delphi, which means they could face each other in the championship with semifinal wins. item.title: William Nylander Reaches Historic Goal Milestone for Maple Leafs
item.description: Maple Leafs William Nylander Getty Toronto Maple Leafs forward William Nylander scored his 300th goal during the Maple Leafs’ win on Saturday night. The Maple Leafs routed the Edmonton Oilers 7-2 in a blowout win on Saturday night for Toronto, who have won four straight games and are looking every bit like a playoff contender at the moment. Nylander scored twice for Toronto, once on the power play and once into an empty net, as Toronto once again gave Edmonton problems at Rogers Place, an arena where they have had plenty of success. William Nylander Reaches 300-Goal Mark After scoring his 299th and 300th career goal, Nylander reached a very elite group of Maple Leafs players who have reached that milestone with the historic hockey club. THAT'S 300 CAREER GOALS FOR WILLIAM NYLANDER 🔵⚪️ pic.twitter.com/AuXRlPQ72h — Sportsnet (@Sportsnet) October 25, 2026 Nylander’s two goals gave him eight for the year as he is on pace for another 40-goal season for the fourth time in his NHL career. He also has 18 points this season. William Nylander’s Maple Leafs Career Nylander was drafted by Toronto with the eighth overall pick in the 2014 NHL Entry Draft, and he has spent his entire NHL career with the Maple Leafs since then. In 763 career regular-season games, Nylander has scored 300 goals and 709 points, while also adding 26 goals and 58 points in 62 career postseason games. The Maple Leafs haven’t had much playoff success during Nylander’s tenure with the club, but it hasn’t been his fault, as he has been playing so well for the club over the years. This season is make-or-break for the Maple Leafs in many ways, as the team is trying to prove to captain Auston Matthews that they are a legitimate Stanley Cup contender and that he should re-sign with the team on a contract extension before his deal with the franchise runs out after next season. Based on how well Toronto has been playing so far this season, it’s fair to say that the Maple Leafs are back, and having Nylander scoring so many goals for the team is certainly helping them, as he is one of the Maple Leafs’ best players and has been ever since he first entered the team’s lineup in 2015. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post William Nylander Reaches Historic Goal Milestone for Maple Leafs appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Loss to Flames Shows Gibson Not off to Hot Start
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Red Wings points-streak came to an end tonight with the Calgary Flames putting three second period goals on John Gibson and the Red Wings’ head tonight, beating them in regulation. It wasn’t Gibson’s prettiest outing, with the veteran netminder giving up four goals on the night in his likely last night at the Saddledome as the Red Wings for the first time since 2023, lost to the Flames 4-1. In a lather Last year, the Red Wings relied heavily on current Columbus Blue Jackets backup Cam Talbot for much of the first two months of the season as Gibson, newly acquired from Anaheim, adjusted to the team in front of him to begin the year. From December on, the Red Wings almost exclusively played Gibson however, with the-then 31-year-old netminder playing the third most games in a single season of his career (57) by the end of the year. Detroit has started Gibson in eight of their first eleven games, with the former Anaheim Ducks netminder accruing a .871 sv%, 3.35 GAA stat line going into the matchup with the Flames. With Gibson in net, the Red Wings are 3-4-1, and in two of those wins have needed to score 3 or more goals in order to achieve victory. “We don’t survive those moments. We don’t score enough, and tonight proved it.” Head coach Todd McLellan said. The Red Wings offensive attack, however, has not been their calling card so far this season, with Detroit relying heavily on team defense to keep them in games. There’s not much Gibson can do about the rest of the skaters on the team putting pucks in net, but he is ranked 52nd amongst NHL netminders in goals saved above expected on the year so far. Hold your horses Backup Daniil Tarasov tweaked something earlier on the Red Wings Pacific Division road trip, which leaves rookie Michal Postava , recalled under emergency conditions, as the Red Wings only other option aside from Gibson for the near future. The Red Wings will next find themselves facing off against the Edmonton Oilers and more importantly, Connor McDavid and Leon Draisatl. McDavid has 33 points in eleven games, and Draisatl is no slouch either, with 23. It would also be Gibson’s third straight start within the last week, if the Red Wings give him the nod. On the other hand, throwing Postava into his first start, on the road, against a high powered Oilers squad seems more like the stuff out of a goalie’s nightmare, though Postava has shown in the past that he is willing to meet just about any challenge. Either way, the Red Wings need to find a better balance in net for Gibson to find his footing. The Red Wings simply do not have the margin for error to be throwing away the first two months of the season waiting for him to find his late season form. item.title: Can players outside Europe win the Ballon d'Or? How France Football award eligibility works
item.description: Can players outside Europe win the Ballon d'Or? How France Football award eligibility works originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Every year, the Ballon d'Or is given out to the greatest football player from the previous season, awarded to the individual who displays the most exemplary performance across the entirety of the criteria period. Traditionally an award for European players from European nations, the eligibility for those who can win the Ballon d'Or has been questioned in recent years, as the talent base spreads further across the globe. Harry Kane, Lamine Yamal, and Kylian Mbappe are the frontrunners to win the 2026 Ballon d'Or, but there are nominees from all around the globe. The Sporting News brings you an overview at who is eligible to win the Ballon d'Or, football's most prestigious individual trophy, and what the history of the award is with regards to geography. MORE: All 30 Ballon d'Or nominees for the 2026 award Who is eligible to win the Ballon d'Or? Beginning with the award's inception in 1956, only players from European nations contracted to European clubs were eligible to win the Ballon d'Or. However, that restrictive nature has evolved over the years to the more inclusive award seen today. In 1995, the Ballon d'Or opened the nominee pool up to players of any nation playing for a European club. Then in 2007, all players in professional football around the world became eligible to win the award. In practice, however, the prize still remains locked into European-based players. Those clubs are not only the most visible but also the most prestigious, and thus performance at the highest level in Europe places players on a pedestal above all others. To date, no player contracted to a club outside of Europe has ever won the Ballon d'Or. The closest was Lionel Messi who secured the final Ballon d'Or of his career in 2023. While he accepted the award as an Inter Miami player, the voting period only considered the time during which he played his final year for Paris Saint-Germain. Thus, this does not officially count, but many still consider it as such. MORE: All-time list of Ballon d'Or winners: Who has won the most? | Which club has the most Ballon d'Or winners? Explaining criteria There are three main criteria that France Football has instructed voters to consider when crafting their list of potential winners: Individual performance, decisive impact, and impressive character Team achievements and collective success Sportsmanship and the player's class, on and off the pitch This means that not only does an individual's raw output matter, but also how well they contribute to their team's collective success, and the manner in which they conduct themselves. What is NOT meant to be considered is past achievements or global status. Originally meant to produce the best player from the last calendar year, France Football recently changed the consideration timeframe to fit the European season. Thus, consideration is taken from the start of August through the end of the competitive summer tournaments. For the 2025/26 season, that means the consideration period begins at the start of league campaigns in August 2025 and runs through the end of the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

item.title: Brentford XI vs Hull City – Predicted lineup and team news
item.description: Brentford XI vs Hull City – Predicted lineup and team news Brentford travel to the MKM Stadium on Sunday afternoon looking to bounce back from their first defeat of the season, a 2-1 loss to Liverpool that cost them two midfielders to red cards. Keith Andrews’ side are sixth in the Premier League with 10 points from seven matches, one point above Sunday’s hosts. Brentford remain unbeaten on their travels this season, though all three of their away matches so far have ended in draws. Brentford’s 13 goals scored and five-goal positive difference from seven matches are among the better underlying numbers in the division outside the top six. Brentford team news Yehor Yarmolyuk and Vitaly Janelt are both suspended after being sent off in last weekend’s defeat to Liverpool, forcing Andrews to completely rebuild his central midfield pairing. Joshua Dasilva (hamstring), Kaye Furo (foot) and Antoni Milambo (knock) are also unavailable, with no fresh doubts reported elsewhere in the squad. Andrews will be without his first-choice central pairing for the first time this season, a blow against a Hull side that has scored three goals from high turnovers in the final third. Club-record signing Mamadou Sangare is set to take one of the vacant central midfield positions, in what will be his first Premier League start since 12 September. Mathias Jensen is expected to partner him in the middle of the park. Jaidon Anthony, Mikkel Damsgaard and Kevin Schade, who has scored three goals from 17 shots this season, are set to continue as the attacking trio behind Igor Thiago, with Michael Kayode and Keane Lewis-Potter retaining their places at full-back either side of Kristoffer Ajer and Schuster in central defence. Brentford predicted lineup Brentford possible starting XI (4-2-3-1): Kelleher; Kayode, Schuster, Ajer, Lewis-Potter; Jensen, Sangare; Anthony, Damsgaard, Schade; Thiago When will the match kick off? The Premier League match kicks off at 14:00 BST on Sunday, 25 October 2026. How to watch Hull City vs Brentford? The match will be broadcast live on Sky Sports in the UK. item.title: Liverpool vs Brighton – Match preview and team news
item.description: Liverpool vs Brighton – Match preview and team news Liverpool host Brighton & Hove Albion in a Premier League Gameweek 8 fixture at Anfield on Sunday, 25 October 2026. Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool are fifth in the table with 12 points from seven matches, four points and two places behind Fabian Hurzeler’s Brighton in third. Brighton have won five of their seven league games, scoring 23 goals and conceding just five, and arrive on the back of a 5-0 win over Crystal Palace. Liverpool’s last meeting with Brighton ended in a 2-1 defeat at the Amex Stadium in March, Danny Welbeck scoring twice. Liverpool vs Brighton – Match preview and team news Date: Sunday, 25 October 2026 Kick-off: 14:00 BST Venue: Anfield Referee: Samuel Barrott Last meeting: Brighton 2-1 Liverpool, 21 March 2026, Premier League Team news Liverpool Dominik Szoboszlai is confirmed out with a hamstring injury, with Victor Munoz also sidelined. Conor Bradley, Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike and Jeremie Frimpong remain long-term absentees, though Bradley Barcola has received a positive fitness update and is in contention to start. Brighton Evan Ferguson, Stefanos Tzimas, Kaoru Mitoma, Femi Azeez and Zadok Yohanna are all unavailable through injury. Jason Steele, Pascal Struijk and Mats Wieffer are doubts, while Yankuba Minteh could feature from the bench on his first appearance of the season. Form Liverpool Liverpool have won three, drawn three and lost one of their seven Premier League matches, scoring nine goals and conceding eight. They have won four of their last five matches across all competitions, with their sole defeat coming against Manchester City. Brighton Brighton have won five, drawn one and lost one of their seven league matches, with 23 goals scored and only five conceded, the best goal difference outside the top two. They have won their last four matches in all competitions, most recently a 5-0 victory over Crystal Palace. Predicted lineups Liverpool possible starting XI (4-2-3-1): Alisson; Araujo, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Kerkez; Nyoni, Mac Allister; Barcola, Wirtz, Ngumoha; Isak Brighton possible starting XI (4-2-3-1): Verbruggen; Kadioglu, Dunk, Vuskovic, Boscagli; Gross, Andres; Gomez, Ayari, De Cuyper; Kostoulas How to watch Liverpool vs Brighton & Hove Albion? The match will be broadcast live in the United Kingdom on Sky Sports. item.title: OTD (25/10/1966): George Herd’s Very Own ‘Match Of The Day’
item.description: The happy couple… George Herd was a fan favourite during his playing days at Roker Park and is still revered at Sunderland AFC nearly sixty years after making his final appearance for the Lads. A hugely energetic and infectious character, plus a popular face on the local non-scene in later years, when he passed away in 2024 there was an outpouring of emotion that proved just how much the community loved him —yet in 1966, it was a very different relationship that was being confirmed. Barbara Wright, a shorthand typist in a Sunderland office, had obviously taken a shine to George, for on Monday 24 October, the pair got married at St Luke’s Church in Pallion. Wanting to keep the ceremony secret, it wasn’t until the following day that most people got to find out about it, when the happy couple appeared in the local press and confirmed that following about six months of planning, everything had gone just as they’d hoped. After the ceremony, they’d gone to their new home in Cleadon before heading to a reception at Barbara’s parents’ house on Westmoor Road, rounding off the celebrations there. The newlyweds had first met at a dance around two years earlier but wanted a low-key event and the only other footballer at the service was George’s fellow Scot Bobby Kerr, who’d previously shared with him club digs on the appropriately-named Hampden Road behind the Fulwell End and Clock Stand. Exactly who it was that had invited him was not clear — maybe Kerr had been invited by the bride, keen to find out what living with her fiancé was going to be like! Whereas the nuptials and gone without a hitch however, the honeymoon period was much shorter than anticipated. Originally given leave of absence until Thursday by manager Ian McColl, Herd was disappointed to learn that his first full day of married life would instead see him having to report back to work, with the previous Saturday’s scheduled fixture against Stoke City having been rearranged at short notice and set to take on Tuesday evening. Initially called off due to a number of international games taking place that weekend, it was the Football League that insisted on the game taking place at the earliest opportunity, and that meant an early end to whatever the Herds had in mind. If there was to be any consolation for George, it was that he at least got to be part of victorious team, pulling off an impressive result against league leaders Stoke City, and that he had a direct hand in the winning goal. Now enjoying service of a different kind, his gift to his teammates was a perfectly-placed corner that was flicked on by George Mulhall and converted by Neil Martin in a 2-1 success. Herd was subsequently given a mark of seven out of ten in The Journal’s match report, and there are more details on the match available here.

Wanting to keep the ceremony secret, it wasn’t until the following day that most people got to find out about it, when the happy couple appeared in the local press and confirmed that following about six months of planning, everything had gone just as they’d hoped. After the ceremony, they’d gone to their new home in Cleadon before heading to a reception at Barbara’s parents’ house on Westmoor Road, rounding off the celebrations there. The newlyweds had first met at a dance around two years earlier but wanted a low-key event and the only other footballer at the service was George’s fellow Scot Bobby Kerr, who’d previously shared with him club digs on the appropriately-named Hampden Road behind the Fulwell End and Clock Stand. Exactly who it was that had invited him was not clear — maybe Kerr had been invited by the bride, keen to find out what living with her fiancé was going to be like! Whereas the nuptials and gone without a hitch however, the honeymoon period was much shorter than anticipated. Originally given leave of absence until Thursday by manager Ian McColl, Herd was disappointed to learn that his first full day of married life would instead see him having to report back to work, with the previous Saturday’s scheduled fixture against Stoke City having been rearranged at short notice and set to take on Tuesday evening. Initially called off due to a number of international games taking place that weekend, it was the Football League that insisted on the game taking place at the earliest opportunity, and that meant an early end to whatever the Herds had in mind. If there was to be any consolation for George, it was that he at least got to be part of victorious team, pulling off an impressive result against league leaders Stoke City, and that he had a direct hand in the winning goal. Now enjoying service of a different kind, his gift to his teammates was a perfectly-placed corner that was flicked on by George Mulhall and converted by Neil Martin in a 2-1 success. Herd was subsequently given a mark of seven out of ten in The Journal’s match report, and there are more details on the match available here.

item.title: Manchester United vs Bournemouth – Match preview and team news
item.description: Manchester United vs Bournemouth – Match preview and team news Manchester United host Bournemouth in a Premier League Gameweek 8 fixture at Old Trafford on Sunday, 25 October 2026. Michael Carrick’s United are 13th in the table with seven points from seven matches, one point and two places above Marco Rose’s Bournemouth. United go into the weekend off the back of a 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League, while Bournemouth beat AC Milan 3-0 in the Europa League in midweek and remain unbeaten in their last six meetings with United, winning none but drawing four and losing two of those encounters. The two sides drew 2-2 when they last met in March. Manchester United vs Bournemouth – Match preview and team news Date: Sunday, 25 October 2026 Kick-off: 14:00 BST Venue: Old Trafford Referee: Jarred Gillett Last meeting: Bournemouth 2-2 Manchester United, March 2026, Premier League Team news Manchester United Manuel Ugarte, Luke Shaw, Benjamin Sesko, Patrick Dorgu and Kobbie Mainoo are all unavailable through injury. Ayden Heaven, Marcus Rashford and Lisandro Martinez missed the Como defeat but could return, and Leny Yoro is available again after a European suspension. Matheus Cunha and Noussair Mazraoui, both substituted at half-time in midweek, are unlikely to retain their places. Bournemouth Alex Toth, Julian Araujo and Alex Scott are all out through injury, while Junior Kroupi is a doubt with a foot problem. Djordje Petrovic returns in goal having been rested for the win over AC Milan, with Adam Smith expected to continue at right-back. Form Manchester United Manchester United have won one, drawn four and lost two of their seven Premier League matches, scoring 10 goals and conceding 10. They are winless in seven matches across all competitions following the midweek defeat to Como. Bournemouth Bournemouth have won one, drawn three and lost three of their seven league matches, with nine goals scored and 13 conceded. They have won their last two matches across all competitions, both with clean sheets, including a 3-0 win over AC Milan that kept their Europa League record unbeaten. Predicted lineups Manchester United possible starting XI (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Yoro, Maguire, De Ligt, Dalot; Tielemans, Baleba; Amad, Fernandes, Rashford; Mbeumo Bournemouth possible starting XI (4-2-3-1): Petrovic; Smith, Hill, Silva, Truffert; Adams, Christie; Rayan, Cook, Tavernier; Evanilson How to watch Manchester United vs Bournemouth? The match will be broadcast live in the United Kingdom on Sky Sports. item.title: Leeds United XI vs Sunderland – Predicted lineup and team news
item.description: Leeds United XI vs Sunderland – Predicted lineup and team news Leeds United travel to the Stadium of Light on Sunday afternoon looking to return to winning ways after being held at home by Manchester United. Daniel Farke’s side are seventh in the Premier League with 10 points from seven matches, six points clear of Sunday’s hosts. Leeds have lost just once in their opening seven fixtures and remain in contention for a top-five finish this season. Farke guided Leeds to the Championship title with 100 points last season, and his side’s composed start back in the Premier League contrasts with a Sunderland team already rooted to the bottom of the table. Leeds United team news Mateo Joseph (knee) and Joe Rodon (hamstring) are both out through injury. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is a doubt with a bruised foot, while Noah Okafor and Anton Stach are both managing adductor issues. Dan James is also a doubt with a back problem. Calvert-Lewin has scored four goals this season and would be a notable miss if he fails to recover in time, while Stach’s 10 created chances have been a key creative outlet behind the front line when he has played. With Calvert-Lewin’s availability in question, Lukas Nmecha is set to lead the line, supported by Harry Wilson and Brenden Aaronson in behind. Ethan Ampadu and Ao Tanaka are expected to continue anchoring midfield, with Jayden Bogle and Gabriel Gudmundsson providing width and defensive cover as wing-backs in Farke’s three-at-the-back system. James Justin, Nico Elvedi and Tarik Muharemovic are set to continue as the back three protecting goalkeeper James Trafford. No further fitness concerns have been reported elsewhere in Farke’s squad. Leeds United predicted lineup Leeds United possible starting XI (3-4-2-1): Trafford; Muharemovic, Elvedi, Justin; Bogle, Ampadu, Tanaka, Gudmundsson; Wilson, Aaronson; Nmecha When will the match kick off? The Premier League match kicks off at 16:30 BST on Sunday, 25 October 2026. How to watch Sunderland vs Leeds United? The match will be broadcast live on Sky Sports in the UK. item.title: Score Predictions - Leeds in the league - can we get a welcome win?
item.description: SUNDERLAND, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 10: General view outside the stadium before the Premier League 2026/27 match between Sunderland and Brighton & Hove Albion at Stadium of Light on October 10, 2026 in Sunderland, England. (Photo by George Wood/Getty Images) Stats at a glance: Leeds (H) Premier League: 25/10/2026 Average home goals predicted: 1.25 Average away goals predicted: 0.62 Confidence of Roker Report’s writers: 5/10 Predicting a win for the Lads: 50% Martin Wanless (Cautious Optimist) says… Score prediction: Sunderland 1 Leeds 1 While a point away in Europe isn’t a bad result, and the performance was a bit better, it wasn’t the type of display that gives you huge confidence that all wrongs have been righted. Our finishing was appalling and we conceded some easy chances too, so we need to hope we make a further step in the right direction today. Leeds are a good side, and it’ll be a tough task to get a result but hopefully we’ll get something. Key differentiator: Robin Roefs — he can keep us in the game Confidence: 3/10 Bold call: Eight yellow cards to be dished out Malc Dugdale (Scarred happy clapper) says… Score prediction: Sunderland 1 Leeds 0 If we can defend better, we showed in the week that we can create a lot. It’s just a case of continuing the progress with both aspects, scoring more than we miss, and we can get back to being ourselves. This will be a tight game for me and while it’s far from a ‘must win’ when we’re still less than ten games into the season, we can’t let the rot set in as this will both impact morale and put Régis Le Bris at risk — he deserves way more time than nine or ten games this season. Hopefully we have Brian Brobbey back and they don’t have Dominic Calvert-Lewin, though both players are subject to speculation about fitness. Let’s get the Stadium of Light back to being a home fortress with a clean sheet and a win, and shut down all these doom-mongers for a short while at least. Key differentiator: Brobbey up front and a resurgent Robin Roefs at the back, and we can take on anyone. Confidence: 5/10 Bold call: One set piece goal will decide this either way, but hopefully in our favour. Jack Howe-Gingell (Eternal optimist) says… Score prediction: Sunderland 2 Leeds 1 It’s one of those people are shouting about being a “must win” but a draw against an in-form Leeds team would be a great result (provided we can go to Coventry and win!). That said, I still fancy us to steal this one. I’m expecting an intense game and I think our fans will be edgy. We showed signs of life against Poznań, but we were too wasteful and it cost us the three points. Leeds will be a much better standard of opponent, and I have to hope we’ll be up to the task. Key differentiator: It’ll feel like a low-key derby on Sunday in my opinion, and despite reservations I think the players will go hard and amp the crowd up. Confidence: 6/10 Bold call: Both of our goals will be from set pieces. “Champion” Will Jones (Heart over head) says… Score predicti

Key differentiator: Robin Roefs — he can keep us in the game Confidence: 3/10 Bold call: Eight yellow cards to be dished out Malc Dugdale (Scarred happy clapper) says… Score prediction: Sunderland 1 Leeds 0 If we can defend better, we showed in the week that we can create a lot. This will be a tight game for me and while it’s far from a ‘must win’ when we’re still less than ten games into the season, we can’t let the rot set in as this will both impact morale and put Régis Le Bris at risk — he deserves way more time than nine or ten games this season. Hopefully we have Brian Brobbey back and they don’t have Dominic Calvert-Lewin, though both players are subject to speculation about fitness. Let’s get the Stadium of Light back to being a home fortress with a clean sheet and a win, and shut down all these doom-mongers for a short while at least. Key differentiator: Brobbey up front and a resurgent Robin Roefs at the back, and we can take on anyone. Confidence: 5/10 Bold call: One set piece goal will decide this either way, but hopefully in our favour. Jack Howe-Gingell (Eternal optimist) says… Score prediction: Sunderland 2 Leeds 1 It’s one of those people are shouting about being a “must win” but a draw against an in-form Leeds team would be a great result (provided we can go to Coventry and win!). That said, I still fancy us to steal this one. I’m expecting an intense game and I think our fans will be edgy. We showed signs of life against Poznań, but we were too wasteful and it cost us the three points. Leeds will be a much better standard of opponent, and I have to hope we’ll be up to the task. Key differentiator: It’ll feel like a low-key derby on Sunday in my opinion, and despite reservations I think the players will go hard and amp the crowd up. Confidence: 6/10 Bold call: Both of our goals will be from set pieces. “Champion” Will Jones (Heart over head) says… Score prediction: Sunderland 1 Leeds 1 A decent point in Poznań on Thursday, and hopefully something we can build on going into Sunday. We’ve had a mixed few weeks, but there were signs of a bit more fight in Europe, and now we need to bring that back to the Stadium of Light. Leeds will make it a proper battle, and I can see this being a tight one with neither side giving much away. The home crowd should give us a lift, but after the European trip, I reckon we might have to settle for a point. Key differentiator: Whoever wins the midfield battle and keeps their head in what could be a scrappy game. Confidence: 5/10 Bold call: Our goal comes from a defender who hasn’t scored for Sunderland before. Matty Foster (Pragmatist) says… Score prediction: Sunderland 0 Leeds 0 I honestly go into this not knowing what to predict. Leeds have a good start, only losing to Arsenal so far. Our league form isn’t great, but I’m trying not to fall into a negative state of mind. They’ve drawn most of their fixtures, and to go entirely “middle of the road”, I’m predicting more of the same again. Key differentiator: Whether Brian Brobbey is playing or not. I don’t envisage us scoring without him. Confidence: 4/10 Bold call: The woodwork will be hit on three or more occasions. Anthony Gair (Depreciating optimist) says… Score prediction: Sunderland 2 Leeds 0 In a game which is a very early “must win” for the mighty wizards, I think we’ll finally start hitting the target against a depleted — and hopefully toothless without Dominic Calvert-Lewin — Leeds side. I think we’ll come out all guns blazing, with the lads absolutely riled up and prepared to die for the shirt. It may lead to a lack of discipline at the back, but I think we’ll have enough to beat this incredibly impressive, Leeds team. Key differentiator: The crowd need to stay patient, support the lads and not get on their backs if they make an error. Confidence: 7/1 0 Bold call: There’ll be a red card in this one. Gary Winter (Glass almost empty) says… Score prediction: Sunderland 1 Leeds 1 It’s probably too soon to be calling out “must win” games this early in the season, as I do believe there’s plenty of time to turn the ship around — the sooner the better, though. Today feels really important, and a win would lift the mounting pressure and buy us just a little breathing space. Dread has already crept in more than it should, so a loss is hard to digest as, rightly or wrongly, panic will crank up several notches. Key differentiator: We could do with a really energetic performance, but after another away trip in Europe, I think the distance travelled will make that difficult. Confidence: 5/10 Bold call: One or more goals scored between 15-30 minutes and one or more goals scored between 45-65 minutes. Brett Lyons-Davis (Gut feeling guy) says… Score prediction: Sunderland 2 Leeds 1 We go again — we need a win, simple as that. The lads did put on a much better performance in Poland and it was refreshing to see some shots and we could/should’ve scored more. Defensively, we did look vulnerable and had Robin Roefs not been on his game, we would be talking about another defeat. Key differentiator: Brian Brobbey. Confidence: 5/10 Bold call: Despite the game being between two tough Northern teams, there will be at least one goal scored by a player wearing gloves. Last game thoughts… Most will agree we should’ve beaten Lech Poznan in the week, but when we opened the game with our lone striker being Timor Tutierov due to wider injuries, scoring goals was always going to be a challenge. I was chuffed at him getting off the mark, but that should’ve been his second, as he made clear in his post-match interviews. Robin Roefs had a blinder and saved our blushes by helping us to an away draw, which many maybe would’ve taken before a ball was kicked since we already have two wins in the competition. A few players also put themselves in the first team shop window again, especially the likes of Jules Ahoka. Today’s challenge will be much sterner and we’ll have to bring all the best bits of our Europa campaign and minimal evidence of our errors and self-destructive moments to get a win against the White Rose. Who’s fit and who isn’t will be vital, too. Last game predictions… Four of the lads correctly called the somewhat deflating draw, but ‘Bold Call’ points were lacking this time around. The form of Grafter Gair continues to impress, with last seasons basement dweller continuing gathering points and holding on to the leaders as we move towards the ten games in the Premier League point. item.title: Fan Focus: What Can Sunderland expect From Daniel Farke’s Leeds?
item.description: POZNAN, POLAND - 2026/10/22: Nordi Mukiele (L), Timur Tuterov (C) and Nilson Angulo (R) of Sunderland celebrate a goal during the UEFA Europa League match between Lech Poznan and AFC Sunderland at Enea Stadium Poznan. Final score: Lech Poznan 1:1 AFC Sunderland. (Photo by Mikolaj Barbanell/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images) Leeds comfortably secured Premier League survival last season, finishing fourteenth after promotion and also reaching the FA Cup semi-finals. How would you assess that first season back and what were your expectations heading into this campaign? A really successful first season back. I would’ve taken seventeenth on goal difference so to have such a strong end to the season was really promising. I don’t think any Leeds fans relaxed until we were mathematically safe, but it was so refreshing to see a Leeds team in the Premier League that didn’t embarrass us week after week and had grit and determination. Leeds currently sit seventh with ten points from their opening seven matches. Have you been surprised by how well the season has started, and has it changed what supporters believe this team can achieve? I’m not completely surprised as I think we handily upgraded the core of our team over the summer. You’ll always have a good start if you’re settled and we smartly upgraded the core of what’s a really settled unit. I think it’s made supporters realise we shouldn’t get drawn into any relegation battle. And some supporters will now believe we can achieve Europe this season. However, I personally disagree, and even though we’re solid, I think limitations mean that mid-table is what our team can realistically achieve. Daniel Farke has now had several years to shape this Leeds side and establish the club back in the Premier League. How highly is he regarded by supporters at this stage, and how has his approach evolved since promotion? It’s a weird one with Farke. I think the ghost of Marcelo Bielsa has hovered over every appointment since, and Daniel has certainly struggled with matching the expectations created by Marcelo. However, Farke is regarded highly — even if grudgingly — by some supporters. He has massively evolved since promotion and is now far more pragmatic and manages to squeeze a lot more out of a unit than he ever seemed to before. Even when we were flying in the Championship, a lot of that seemed to be because of the players rather than him. However, despite how well he’s doing and has evolved, I think there still is a ceiling if he want to progress beyond just being solid. Saying that, though, he’s a very steady captain of the ship and you need to appreciate what you’ve got, because things could go downhill rapidly without him. Leeds drew 1-1 with Manchester United last weekend, having also beaten Newcastle 4-1 and taken a point away at Brighton already this season. Which performance has given you the most encouragement so far? That point away at Brighton is looking better by the week! But I think the Newcastle
item.content:encoded: POZNAN, POLAND - 2026/10/22: Nordi Mukiele (L), Timur Tuterov (C) and Nilson Angulo (R) of Sunderland celebrate a goal during the UEFA Europa League match between Lech Poznan and AFC Sunderland at Enea Stadium Poznan. Final score: Lech Poznan 1:1 AFC Sunderland. (Photo by Mikolaj Barbanell/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images) Leeds comfortably secured Premier League survival last season, finishing fourteenth after promotion and also reaching the FA Cup semi-finals. How would you assess that first season back and what were your expectations heading into this campaign? A really successful first season back. I would’ve taken seventeenth on goal difference so to have such a strong end to the season was really promising. I don’t think any Leeds fans relaxed until we were mathematically safe, but it was so refreshing to see a Leeds team in the Premier League that didn’t embarrass us week after week and had grit and determination. Leeds currently sit seventh with ten points from their opening seven matches. Have you been surprised by how well the season has started, and has it changed what supporters believe this team can achieve? I’m not completely surprised as I think we handily upgraded the core of our team over the summer. You’ll always have a good start if you’re settled and we smartly upgraded the core of what’s a really settled unit. I think it’s made supporters realise we shouldn’t get drawn into any relegation battle. And some supporters will now believe we can achieve Europe this season. However, I personally disagree, and even though we’re solid, I think limitations mean that mid-table is what our team can realistically achieve. Daniel Farke has now had several years to shape this Leeds side and establish the club back in the Premier League. How highly is he regarded by supporters at this stage, and how has his approach evolved since promotion? It’s a weird one with Farke. I think the ghost of Marcelo Bielsa has hovered over every appointment since, and Daniel has certainly struggled with matching the expectations created by Marcelo. However, Farke is regarded highly — even if grudgingly — by some supporters. He has massively evolved since promotion and is now far more pragmatic and manages to squeeze a lot more out of a unit than he ever seemed to before. Even when we were flying in the Championship, a lot of that seemed to be because of the players rather than him. However, despite how well he’s doing and has evolved, I think there still is a ceiling if he want to progress beyond just being solid. Saying that, though, he’s a very steady captain of the ship and you need to appreciate what you’ve got, because things could go downhill rapidly without him. Leeds drew 1-1 with Manchester United last weekend, having also beaten Newcastle 4-1 and taken a point away at Brighton already this season. Which performance has given you the most encouragement so far? That point away at Brighton is looking better by the week! But I think the Newcastle one is still the most encouraging. Our biggest weakness is probably our attacking unit (Dominic Calvert-Lewin aside) and so any performance where we score goals is encouraging. The Manchester United result is weirdly pretty disappointing as right now, our biggest rivals feel there for the taking. The club made seven additions during the summer, including James Trafford, Harry Wilson, Tarik Muharemović and Nico Elvedi. How happy were you with the transfer window and which of the new signings has impressed you most? We’ve had our fair share of bad transfer windows so Leeds fans are often wary and usually assume we’re going to “mess things up” (deadline day has been particularly painful). However, on reflection, it was a great transfer window and really created a solid unit that will always make you competitive. Muharemović was an inspired signing and Nico Elvedi also looks like a great one. Harry Wilson the only one that has been pretty disappointing so far and doesn’t look quite up to our intensity. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is Leeds’ leading scorer with four Premier League goals and has earned an England recall, although he’s a doubt for today through injury. How important has he become to this team? I can’t sing DCL’s praises enough. He’s the perfect striker in his all-round play and we look far better when he plays. People talk about his finishing but when he does everything right, and still scores, you can’t really complain. If he doesn’t play vs Sunderland, we’ll be far worse off for it. Calvert-Lewin, Anton Stach and Noah Okafor are all major doubts for the trip to Sunderland, while Joe Rodon remains out, although Daniel James is back in contention. How much would those potential absences affect Leeds today? Massively. DCL is so important for us. Stach is an absolute monster in the middle and Okafor is our main spark in attack. If all three are out, that’s 100% advantage Sunderland but Farke has often exaggerated things and plays mind games with these things. Leeds have recently been using a 3-4-2-1 system, with Ethan Ampadu and Ao Tanaka playing important roles through the middle. What are the biggest strengths of this side tactically, and where are they still vulnerable? Biggest strengths: central midfield, centre backs, wing backs. A very solid unit that always looks competitive even when not playing that well. Our set pieces and physicality are also very suited for the Premier League. Weaknesses: DCL and Okafor are great, but in attack it often can look like we don’t have much of a plan except to launch it up to DCL, and can look flat. If you also allow us to dominate and sit on the counter we lack creativity, we can look far stronger on the counter. I still think Farke is limited in tactical nous compared to the best managers in this league and this lack of tactical flexibility can be exposed. Sunderland took four points from Leeds last season, drawing 1-1 at the Stadium of Light before winning 1-0 at Elland Road. From what you’ve seen of Sunderland since, where do you think they can cause Leeds the most problems on Sunday? From sitting back and hitting us on the counter. Régis Le Bris has looked tactically superior in a few of the games and if we don’t get an early goal or Sunderland do, it could be a tough watch with us trying to break Sunderland down. Finally, what type of game are you expecting at the Stadium of Light? Who do you think could be the difference-maker for Leeds and what is your score prediction? I expect a very cagey game. Sunderland need the win and we will be pretty tight as always in defence. I’d love to see Wilson finally pay back his big wages and show how he can be a difference maker in attack, especially with some of our big attackers injured. I’ve put 1-0 to Sunderland on my Super 6, but I’ve got to back my team if I’m representing us here, so I’m going to go 0-1 Leeds, with the winner being a Wilson free kick.

item.title: Newcastle United XI vs Crystal Palace – Predicted lineup and team news
item.description: Newcastle United XI vs Crystal Palace – Predicted lineup and team news Newcastle United travel to Selhurst Park on Sunday afternoon looking to halt a run of three defeats in their last four Premier League matches. Matthias Jaissle’s side are 11th in the table with eight points from seven games, having won three of their opening five matches in charge before a recent downturn that includes a 4-1 defeat to Coventry City and a 1-0 loss to Aston Villa. Newcastle have scored just four goals across their last four matches, a marked drop-off from the attacking form that marked the early weeks of Jaissle’s reign. Newcastle sit third-bottom of the Premier League’s form table over the last five matches, underlining the scale of the task facing Jaissle this weekend. Newcastle United team news Jacob Ramsey is unlikely to feature because of a thigh injury, with Jaissle keen not to rush the midfielder back into the squad. Tino Livramento (knee) and Ewen Jaouen (thigh) are also out. Matias Fernandez-Pardo is a doubt with illness and Anthony Elanga with a thigh issue, and both will be assessed closer to kick-off. Harvey Barnes leads the squad for assists and big chances created this season, while only Elanga and Joe Willock have scored more than once. If Elanga is passed fit, he is expected to continue on the left of an attacking trio, but Jacob Murphy and William Osula look the more likely options to support Wissa if he is unavailable. Nico Gonzalez and Joelinton are set to continue as the central midfield pairing, with Lewis Miley, Malick Thiaw, Sven Botman and Lewis Hall forming the back four protecting goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek. Newcastle United predicted lineup Newcastle United possible starting XI (4-2-3-1): Hornicek; Miley, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Gonzalez, Joelinton; Murphy, Osula, Barnes; Wissa When will the match kick off? The Premier League match kicks off at 14:00 BST on Sunday, 25 October 2026. How to watch Crystal Palace vs Newcastle United? The match will be broadcast live on Sky Sports in the UK. item.title: Ebola in Nigeria: Fears contacts could test positive mount
item.description: •Prof Tomori asks authorities to prepare •Nigeria’s real test is inside its hospitals •Can health workers count on running water, sanitizer, protective equipment? By Chioma Obinna The tap is there. But is there water? The sanitiser dispenser is mounted on the wall. But is it filled? And if a patient walks into a hospital with symptoms that raise suspicion of a dangerous infection, will the health worker attending to that patient have the protective equipment needed to stay safe? These questions may sound routine. But as Nigeria confronts a confirmed case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease, they go to the heart of a more difficult question: how prepared are the country’s hospitals to prevent another outbreak? Nigeria has been here before. The 2014 Ebola outbreak tested the country’s ability to detect an imported infection, trace contacts and prevent wider transmission. The COVID-19 pandemic later exposed the importance of hand hygiene, personal protective equipment and infection prevention and control in health facilities. Emergency measures were introduced. Isolation facilities were established, surveillance was strengthened and health workers were trained to respond to infectious threats. But what happens when the emergency passes? Do the taps still run? Are protective supplies replenished? Can hospitals still isolate suspected cases safely? And do health workers have the equipment and practical support to implement the precautions they have been trained to observe? For infectious disease experts, Nigeria’s latest Ebola alert is a reminder that preparedness cannot be measured by emergency announcements alone. It must be evident in the wards, consultation rooms and emergency units where patients first seek care. According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), the patient, a woman with a recent travel history involving Uganda, developed symptoms on October 7 and sought treatment at a private hospital in Abuja on October 11. item.content:encoded: •Prof Tomori asks authorities to prepare •Nigeria’s real test is inside its hospitals •Can health workers count on running water, sanitizer, protective equipment? By Chioma Obinna The tap is there. But is there water? The sanitiser dispenser is mounted on the wall. But is it filled? And if a patient walks into a hospital with symptoms that raise suspicion of a dangerous infection, will the health worker attending to that patient have the protective equipment needed to stay safe? These questions may sound routine. But as Nigeria confronts a confirmed case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease, they go to the heart of a more difficult question: how prepared are the country’s hospitals to prevent another outbreak? Nigeria has been here before. The 2014 Ebola outbreak tested the country’s ability to detect an imported infection, trace contacts and prevent wider transmission. The COVID-19 pandemic later exposed the importance of hand hygiene, personal protective equipment and infection prevention and control in health facilities. Emergency measures were introduced. Isolation facilities were established, surveillance was strengthened and health workers were trained to respond to infectious threats. But what happens when the emergency passes? Do the taps still run? Are protective supplies replenished? Can hospitals still isolate suspected cases safely? And do health workers have the equipment and practical support to implement the precautions they have been trained to observe? For infectious disease experts, Nigeria’s latest Ebola alert is a reminder that preparedness cannot be measured by emergency announcements alone. It must be evident in the wards, consultation rooms and emergency units where patients first seek care. One confirmed case, a nationwide test Nigeria’s latest Ebola alert followed the confirmation of an imported case of Bundibugyo virus disease in the Federal Capital Territory on October 20, 2026. According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), the patient, a woman with a recent travel history involving Uganda, developed symptoms on October 7 and sought treatment at a private hospital in Abuja on October 11. Laboratory tests confirmed the infection on October 20. Authorities identified 44 contacts for monitoring, including people who might have been exposed during the patient’s healthcare visits and travel. The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) activated its incident management system, while surveillance and infection-prevention measures were strengthened. By October 23, the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate, said the patient was showing signs of recovery. There was no evidence of community transmission in the information released at that point, although investigations and contact monitoring were continuing. Genomic analysis also found that the virus detected in Nigeria was genetically related to the strain identified in Kenya’s index case. Pate cautioned that this similarity did not, by itself, establish a direct epidemiological link between the two patients or explain precisely how the infection reached Nigeria. The response is therefore unfolding on two fronts. Authorities must establish whether anyone else has been infected, while ensuring that hospitals can recognise and safely manage any suspected cases that emerge. Second responsibility That second responsibility is particularly important. A patient with fever, headache, vomiting or diarrhoea may have any of several illnesses. But when the symptoms are accompanied by a relevant exposure history, health workers must know what questions to ask, whom to notify and how to protect themselves and others while the patient is assessed. An outbreak may be detected by a laboratory, but preventing further transmission also depends on what happens at the patient’s first point of contact with the health system. When the basics cannot be taken for granted Running water, soap, hand sanitisers, cleaning materials, protective equipment and safe waste disposal rarely command the attention given to emergency operations centres or laboratory testing. Yet these ordinary provisions underpin the safe delivery of healthcare. A tap without water cannot support handwashing. An empty sanitiser dispenser offers little protection. Personal protective equipment that is missing when needed can leave a health worker unable to follow the precautions required when caring for a suspected infectious case. The problem is not necessarily that every Nigerian hospital lacks these facilities. It is that their availability, functionality and reliability cannot be assumed. A UNICEF Nigeria WASH Gender Landscape Analysis published in January 2025 reported that only six per cent of healthcare facilities assessed had basic water, sanitation and hygiene services. The figure relates to the facilities covered by the assessment, rather than every hospital in the country, but it highlights a significant infrastructure challenge. For Ebola preparedness, the implications are immediate. Infection prevention is not simply a matter of displaying instructions on a hospital wall. It requires dependable water supplies, adequate consumables, appropriate protective equipment, trained staff and systems that ensure these resources are available where and when they are needed. Items to stop virus The Medical and Dental Consultants’ Association of Nigeria (MDCAN), through its leadership, has called on hospital managements to provide running water, hand sanitisers, infrared thermometers, adequate personal protective equipment, other essential consumables and suitable isolation facilities. The association has also advocated the reactivation of infection prevention and control committees and emergency drills to test the readiness of healthcare workers. Its warning is straightforward, doctors and other health workers should not attend to suspected Ebola patients without appropriate protective equipment or manage them in open wards where other patients and staff could be exposed. These are not special provisions to be considered only when Ebola appears. They are basic requirements for a health system expected to manage infectious diseases safely. Training is not enough The Federal Government had announced that it is strengthening detection, laboratory capacity, case management and public communication as part of the response. “All hospitals should be sensitised and health workers be aware and, when there are suspected cases, to notify public health authorities,” Pate said. The government has also announced plans to reinforce infection prevention and control protocols and train health workers to identify suspected cases, protect themselves and notify the relevant authorities promptly. But experts say training alone cannot make a hospital ready. A health worker may understand the correct procedure and still be unable to follow it if protective equipment is unavailable, water is unreliable or there is no appropriate space to isolate a suspected patient. In an interview with Sunday Vanguard, Professor Dimie Ogoina, a professor of medicine and infectious diseases at Bayelsa Medical University, stressed the need to equip health workers with both the knowledge and resources required to prevent transmission. He warned that an imported case could lead to further spread if contacts became infected and passed the virus to others before preventive measures were put in place. Transmission could also occur during hospital visits or care if appropriate infection prevention and control measures were not observed. “Supporting healthcare workers in adhering to IPC through training and the provision of IPC resources will help promote the adoption of these measures,” he said. For Ogoina, the priority is to ensure that the country’s emergency response translates into practical readiness at federal and state levels. He called for active case searches, effective contact
