item.title: Blaming opposition for hunger is delusional — Atiku
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike & Olayinka Ajayi Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has accused President Bola Tinubu of shifting responsibility for Nigeria’s economic hardship to the opposition, insisting that the administration must account for its record ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Read Also: 2027: ‘They created the hunger’ — Tinubu slams opponents at Kaduna rally Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), was reacting to Tinubu’s remark at the APC campaign flag-off in Kaduna on Saturday that the opposition created hunger and poverty in the country. In a statement issued by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku described the President’s comment as “either delusion or a staggering case of political amnesia”. “The APC governed Nigeria for eight years before you took office. You have added another three and a half years. Nigerians know who has been in power, and hardship did not begin when the opposition started talking about it. Stop insulting their intelligence and answer for your record,” he said. Atiku accused Tinubu’s administration of worsening the hardship faced by Nigerians, arguing that the President could not dismiss concerns about the cost of living by blaming political opponents. He also criticised Tinubu’s planned inauguration of a section of the Abuja-Kaduna Expressway, alleging that the ceremony showed how disconnected the President was from the daily realities of Nigerians. “A road cannot be completed with a speech or a ribbon cutting ceremony,” he said. The former Vice President challenged the administration to explain the removal of the petrol subsidy and the depreciation of the naira, which he claimed had fallen from about ₦471 to ₦1,329 to the dollar. He also cited a World Bank estimate that 63 per cent of Nigerians would be below the national poverty line in 2026, accusing the government of presiding over rising poverty. Atiku further questioned the extension of the 2024 budget into 2025 alongside a separate 2025 budget, as well as what he described as ₦7.13 trillion recorded under “energy security” in 2024 and ₦11.2 trillion in NNPC pipeline-related spending. The post Blaming opposition for hunger is delusional — Atiku appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tinubu flags-off campaign, blasts opposition, backs APC governors against Rainbow Coalition
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru President Bola Tinubu on Saturday opened the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign in Kaduna with a direct attack on his political opponents, accusing them of creating the hunger and poverty currently facing Nigerians, while asking supporters to mobilise for his re-election on January 16, 2027. Read Also: 2027: ‘They created the hunger’ — Tinubu slams opponents at Kaduna rally The President described the opposition as failures and angry people who rely on heckling instead of constructive policy, saying they have nothing to offer the country. Addressing the crowd at the campaign flag-off, Tinubu said: “I hear my opponents talking about hunger and poverty. Who created it? They did. They created the hunger. They created the poverty we are trying to eradicate.” He defended his administration’s record, saying: “We pay salaries regularly. Our governors are working. I am proud of them. They are developing.” Tinubu told supporters that a second term would deliver “prosperity, continuity, progress and development,” adding: “To you, the children of our country, it is a promise of second-term prosperity. You will not regret going to vote.” He repeatedly asked the audience to confirm that they possessed their Permanent Voter Cards, saying: “Do you have your PVC? Do you have your PVC? Show your hands up.” The President also dismissed opposition criticism as anger arising from failure. “This is not a matter of hunger; this is not a matter of anger either. Our opponents are angry because they are failures. They have nothing to offer you but heckling,” he said. “We have prosperity, consistency, growth, recovery and opportunity. I assure you,” Tinubu declared. Your future is in your hands; the fingerprint will reflect it.” On the pledge by former Vice President and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, to bring back petrol subsidy if elected, Tinubu said the removal of fuel subsidy belonged to the past and pledged a future free of corruption and economic sabotage. “Fuel subsidy is in our past. item.dc:creator: Oboh
item.content:encoded: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru President Bola Tinubu on Saturday opened the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign in Kaduna with a direct attack on his political opponents, accusing them of creating the hunger and poverty currently facing Nigerians, while asking supporters to mobilise for his re-election on January 16, 2027. Read Also: 2027: ‘They created the hunger’ — Tinubu slams opponents at Kaduna rally The President described the opposition as failures and angry people who rely on heckling instead of constructive policy, saying they have nothing to offer the country. Addressing the crowd at the campaign flag-off, Tinubu said: “I hear my opponents talking about hunger and poverty. Who created it? They did. They created the hunger. They created the poverty we are trying to eradicate.” He defended his administration’s record, saying: “We pay salaries regularly. Our governors are working. I am proud of them. They are developing.” Tinubu told supporters that a second term would deliver “prosperity, continuity, progress and development,” adding: “To you, the children of our country, it is a promise of second-term prosperity. You will not regret going to vote.” He repeatedly asked the audience to confirm that they possessed their Permanent Voter Cards, saying: “Do you have your PVC? Do you have your PVC? Show your hands up.” The President also dismissed opposition criticism as anger arising from failure. “This is not a matter of hunger; this is not a matter of anger either. Our opponents are angry because they are failures. They have nothing to offer you but heckling,” he said. “We have prosperity, consistency, growth, recovery and opportunity. I assure you,” Tinubu declared. In apparent support of the APC governors’ position against the call by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, for a rainbow coalition, Tinubu urged voters to come out “massively” on January 16, 2027, to re-elect him and support APC candidates across the board. “Come January 2027, January 16, you must go out massively to elect me again. APC all the way. APC for our governors. APC for our senators. APC for our honourable members of the House of Representatives and all houses of assembly,” he said. He added: “Your prosperity is here. Your future is in your hands; the fingerprint will reflect it.” On the pledge by former Vice President and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, to bring back petrol subsidy if elected, Tinubu said the removal of fuel subsidy belonged to the past and pledged a future free of corruption and economic sabotage. “Fuel subsidy is in our past. No more corruption. No more falsification of invoices. No more lies. No more smuggling of wealth,” he said. He praised APC governors, saying: “Out of 36 of them, I can see the development strides they are making in their various states,” and reiterated his promise of “a better tomorrow.” The Kaduna rally marks the formal launch of the APC’s campaign for Tinubu’s re-election ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election. He cautioned voters to remain vigilant against lies and ensure that their choices are accurately reflected through fingerprinting. President Tinubu acknowledged the historical significance of Kaduna State, where political leaders converged before independence. He offered prayers for the souls of departed leaders, asking God to forgive their sins and grant them peaceful repose. President Tinubu promised that voters would not regret supporting his re-election, under the pillars of growth, recovery and opportunity. Key corrections Speaking earlier, the Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima said “Nigeria needs this finest servant to stand together.” According to him: “What we have done is to fight for the survival of this nation. So, allow me, Your Excellencies, distinguished ladies and gentlemen, to reintroduce ourselves to you and show you that you do not have allies as sincere as we are. “We were able to keep this country together and defy the predictions of those who had predicted economic failure because we worked together. “Almost four years ago, you spoke eloquently, sincerely, boldly and decisively to elect a change-maker, His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, as President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria. “We didn’t win that election because we were wise, far from it. We didn’t win that election because we were rich, and we didn’t win that election because we were educated. We didn’t win that election because we were the best speakers. We won because you saw the options before you and knew, without a doubt, that the alternative was a calamity.’’ “And for the good people of Kaduna State, we have seen why you, too, were told to renew the mandate of the APC and give His Excellency, Governor Uba Sani a mandate to redeem the fortunes of this great state. “His wisdom has made Kaduna State a unified place, where the man from Zonkwa sees the man from Zaria as a brother, and where the dividends of our democracy are felt in Kachia as they are in metropolitan Kaduna. “This is the legacy of the APC in Kaduna State. This is the mandate we have come to ask you to renew: a second term for the APC, from top to bottom.” Why Kaduna? On why Kaduna was chosen, the Vice President said: “We have the courage to come to Kaduna State today because we have kept our promise and never reneged on it. “First and foremost, we promised to restore the glory of Kaduna State as a national centre of learning. Did we deliver on that? We have brought you the Federal University of Applied Sciences, Kachia, haven’t we? We have carried forward the transition to the Federal University of Education, Zaria, haven’t we? “We have established state vocational institutes in Rigachikun, Soba and Samaru Kataf, with over 4,000 graduates. “We have committed all our education funding through NELFUND to support hundreds of thousands of students in universities, haven’t we? So, the APC is a party that delivers on its promises. “And you can bear witness that in 2015 and 2019, President Tinubu stood solidly behind the late President Muhammadu Buhari, securing his first- and second-term victories. “This is the reason why we have all stood with him to declare our support for Alhaji Bola Tinubu. This is a man of honour, a man of integrity and a man of honour.” Vanguard News The post Tinubu flags-off campaign, blasts opposition, backs APC governors against Rainbow Coalition appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 5 Most Perfect 1980s Games That Nobody Remembers
item.description: The 1980s wasn't the decade video games were born; the origins of the medium go back a further 20 years, through the likes of Spacewar! and Pong . But it was in the 1980s that video games grew up, exploding in popularity and complexity and establishing many of their defining stars. It was the decade that gave us Mario and Zelda, Pac-Man, Final Fantasy, Prince of Persia, and SimCity. But it also gave us some much more obscure titles that have since fallen by the wayside. Here are five fantastic '80s games that might have been forgotten, but still have something to teach us.

item.title: Alvarez apologises to Atletico fans after summer exit attempt
item.description: Julian Alvarez apologised to Atletico Madrid fans on Saturday for trying to leave the club during the summer, admitting he understands why supporters were angry with him. The Argentina international was heavily linked with Barcelona this summer and said during the World Cup he thought it would be best if Atletico sold him. The Rojiblancos refused to accept an offer from the Catalan giants and Alvarez was whistled and jeered by the club’s own fans at the start of the season. However, the tension has gradually eased and Alvarez netted his first goals of the season this week, firstly against Stuttgart in the Champions League and then on Saturday helping the club beat Deportivo La Coruna 1-0. “I wanted to apologise to our people for my words during the World Cup,” Alvarez told Movistar. “The truth is it was a mistake on my part, both in how I expressed myself and the timing. Above all because I understand people’s anger — I would have been angry too, as a fan. “And also because of how they’ve stuck by me and supported me all these years and in these last few weeks. They’ve been very generous, and I really value that.” Atletico signed the 26-year-old from Manchester City in 2024 and he has become a key figure for Diego Simeone’s side over the previous two seasons. Alvarez put in his brightest display of the season against Deportivo and his goal split the teams at the Metropolitano stadium. “I’m starting to feel good… I’m grateful to all my teammates because they’ve supported me,” continued Alvarez. “They’ve really stuck by me throughout this whole time… and I’m working to improve. “I’ve felt better in these last few matches… both physically and with the ball.” AFP The post Alvarez apologises to Atletico fans after summer exit attempt appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Okpebholo threatens to sign death warrant of condemned kidnappers, cultists if …
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu, BENIN CITY Governor Monday Okpebholo of Edo State has said he would not hesitate to sign the death of the four convicted Vegetable Market kidnappers if they did not appeal against the judgment within the stipulated time. Read Also: Court orders speedy trial of 5 suspected kidnappers of NYSC members in Imo State He said even if they appealed they were just postponing what would still come on them. Speaking during a fellowship at God’s People Worldwide Prayer Ministry, while reviewing his administration’s efforts to curb kidnapping, cultism and other violent crimes in Edo State, said insecurity was one of the biggest worries he met on assuming office. Okpebholo said that he raised the state of the roads and the security situation with President Bola Tinubu at their meeting who he said give him the approval to resolve the issues. The governor said that when the gunmen struck at the Vegetable Market in Benin City, he called the President, who asked if he could handle it, and he said he could. “I called the Commissioner of Police and told him I wanted these guys arrested, because I already have an approval from God, and they were caught within that time. “They are already sentenced to death, and I pray they don’t appeal the judgment. Even when they appeal the judgment, they are only delaying time. If within the days stipulated, they don’t appeal, I will execute,” he said. An Edo State Special Criminal Court on September 29 2026 sentenced four defendants to death for the abduction of a woman at the Vegetable Market along Airport Road, Benin City. The governor said that before he began the campaign against kidnapping and cultism, he met prominent traditional rulers across the state to warn them against interceding for anyone involved in the crimes. He recalled many strange incidents linked to spiritual forces after his administration pulled down a building associated with a cult group: “A black bird died in my office when I demolished their building. A vulture also died in my bed while contesting for governorship,” he said. Founder of God’s People Worldwide Prayer Ministry, Apostle Ehijele Umuahia, during the event urged church members to vote for the governor and his preferred candidates in the 2027 elections. Citing Proverbs 29:2, he told the congregation that prayer for the governor should go together with active participation in the electoral process. Christians, he said, should come out in large numbers to vote. Umuahia described Governor Okpebholo as a humble man whose commitment to the things of God predates his time as governor. He said he has known him for over 15 years, from the days of the late Chief Tony Anenih. “Whenever Chief Tony Anenih came to visit me, he was one of those who accompanied him. That was how we came to know each other,” he said. Vanguard News The post Okpebholo threatens to sign death warrant of condemned kidnappers, cultists if … appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: New York Archdiocese agrees to pay $800m to sex abuse victims
item.description: The Archdiocese of New York said Saturday it had agreed to a settlement in which the church would pay more than $800 million to hundreds of victims of sexual abuse by clergy. The agreement, to be formally signed in early November, marks the end of years of negotiations with lawyers representing the plaintiffs, as the American Catholic Church has been mired in sexual abuse scandals since the early 2000s. “We are on the verge of being able to, please God, bring some measure of healing and reconciliation to all victim-survivors,” New York Archbishop Ronald Hicks wrote in an email sent to his priests and forwarded to AFP by the archdiocese. According to The New York Times, which broke the story, each of the approximately 1,300 victims will receive at least $250,000, and potentially more depending on the severity of the abuse suffered. The Archdiocese of New York, which covers Manhattan, Staten Island, the Bronx and several counties north of the city, will now be able to “turn its full attention once again to its mission of preaching the Gospel, healing the sick, caring for the poor and needy, welcoming the stranger, and educating our children,” Hicks’ email said. Hicks was appointed bishop last year by Pope Leo XIV, replacing the influential conservative Cardinal Timothy Dolan. Before his departure, Dolan had announced the creation of a $300 million fund to compensate sexual abuse victims. In the 2000s, press investigations revealed that Catholic priests in the United States had committed sexual abuse against thousands of children over several decades, and that church leaders had often covered up these cases or transferred the offending priests instead of reporting them to civil authorities. Dioceses across the country have had to pay hundreds of millions of dollars in damages, and programs have been created to compensate victims without going to trial. Last June, the Archdiocese of San Francisco announced it had reached an agreement to pay $395 million to about 530 victims of sexual abuse committed by its clergy in order to settle their lawsuits. AFP The post New York Archdiocese agrees to pay $800m to sex abuse victims appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Alvarez fires Atletico to win against Deportivo
item.description: Julian Alvarez continued on his road to redemption by scoring the only goal as Atletico Madrid beat Deportivo La Coruna 1-0 on Saturday to close the gap on La Liga leaders Barcelona to two points. Diego Simeone’s side are second, with champions Barca hosting Real Madrid, third, in the Clasico at Camp Nou on Sunday. Alvarez netted for the second consecutive game, having grabbed his first of the season in Atletico’s 1-1 Champions League draw at Stuttgart in midweek. Atletico supporters hounded Alvarez during his first appearances this season after he tried to force his way out of the club in the summer, but the tension has gradually cooled. Home fans at the Metropolitano stadium directed a few whistles at the team in general after a slow start, with Deportivo having the best chance of the first half. Atletico goalkeeper Jan Oblak saved well from Lorenzo Amatucci, while at the other end Diego Simeone’s side lacked spark. Early in the second half Alvarez found the breakthrough. Alejandro Grimaldo fired in a dangerous low pass towards the far post, where the Argentina international turned it over the line. Alvarez came close to a second after a slick team move, with Alex Baena slipping him in, but Depor goalkeeper Leo Roman saved the striker’s attempted lob with his face. The former Manchester City striker looked much closer to his best form in this outing after struggling with some fitness problems earlier in the campaign. Alexander Sorloth lashed narrowly over from a tight angle as Atletico sought to kill off the game, unsuccessfully. Deportivo might have levelled in stoppage time with Kevin Sanchez volleying well wide from Adama Traore’s cross when well placed to trouble Oblak. The Galicians’ best chance came with virtually the last kick of the game, with Oblak saving from Sanchez on his line, when the forward seemed destined to score. Earlier, Georges Mikautadze snatched a late 2-1 win for Villarreal in a derby clash against Valencia, who had midfielder Harvey Elliott sent off as both sides finished with 10 men. The Yellow Submarine came from behind to triumph, climbing into mid-table and leaving Javier Aguirre’s Los Che 19th, in the relegation zone. Pepelu sent Valencia ahead from the penalty spot in the first half before American defender Alex Freeman headed the visitors level at Mestalla stadium after 69 minutes. Inigo Perez’s Villarreal had Pape Gueye sent off when the Senegal international hit Jose Gaya in the face with his elbow. However, English midfielder Elliott, on loan from Liverpool, was soon dismissed for two quick yellow cards for apparent dissent. Villarreal striker Mikautadze broke through in stoppage time, racing through and finishing with aplomb to claim the three points. AFP The post Alvarez fires Atletico to win against Deportivo appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Blue Planet III is keeping the rough edges in the age of AI
item.description: BBC's Blue Planet III is looking to prove its authenticity by leaving in the less-than-perfect shots. Previous incarnations of the nature series were defined by their gorgeous, crystal-clear footage that seemed almost too good to be real. But one dead giveaway of AI is when things look too polished and seamless. To counter that, Blue Planet III goes warts and all. Executive Producer Elizabeth White told The Guardian in the past, "the amount of plankton and things" floating in the water would have caused them to cut a shot. Or "we might have framed out a boat or a buoy or gone: 'Oh, actually … the water conditions are not really good enough … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: European football: Lazio beat Parma to top Serie A; Dortmund lead Bundesliga
item.description: Lazio win 2-1 while Roma draw 3-3 with Napoli Beier gives Dortmund win over Eintracht Frankfurt Lazio climbed to the top of Serie A with a 2-1 home win ⁠over Parma ⁠as Roma ​twice came from behind to secure a 3-3 draw with Napoli in a pulsating clash in Naples. Lazio have 22 points from their eight matches this ⁠season and are three points clear of champions Inter Milan, who have played a game fewer and host Fiorentina on Sunday. Lazio opened the scoring in the 50th minute as Kenneth Taylor ⁠struck his first of the season, before Parma’s Diego Carlos put the ball into his own net trying ​to cut out a cross. item.title: Obama blasts Trump’s ‘chaos and cruelty’ while campaigning for Democrats
item.description: Former US president Barack Obama delivered a scathing critique of his successor, Donald Trump, at a rally Saturday in Ohio to support Democratic candidates ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. “After two years of chaos and cruelty and corruption and incompetence, the likes of which we have not seen in the modern era, you get a chance to say, ‘Enough is enough,'” Obama declared in Cleveland. “We are voting for change right here in Ohio.” The 65-year-old Democrat blamed the Trump administration for the rising cost of living, a top voter concern amid soaring fuel prices. “The current president chose to make a series of bad decisions,” Obama said. “Most importantly, he decided to start an unnecessary war that nobody asked for.” Obama also urged voters to cast their ballots as soon as possible since early voting is already open in this northern industrial state. “Don’t procrastinate, don’t equivocate,” Obama said. The former president retains considerable popularity among the Democratic base, which he is keen to leverage to support his party’s candidates in the upcoming crucial elections that will decide control of Congress. In Ohio, former Democratic senator Sherrod Brown will attempt a comeback against incumbent Republican Senator Jon Husted, while the race for governor will be contested between Democrat Amy Acton and Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, a former presidential candidate in 2024. Polls for Ohio give Democrats a slight lead in both those races, but the results are expected to be close. Nationally, polls also suggest that Democrats could regain control of the House of Representatives but face a much more competitive contest for the Senate. After Cleveland, Obama will head north to Michigan this evening for a rally in Detroit alongside Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic Senate candidate. While both of Michigan’s Senate seats are currently held by Democrats, El-Sayed, from the party’s left wing, is in a close race with Republican Mike Rogers. AFP The post Obama blasts Trump’s ‘chaos and cruelty’ while campaigning for Democrats appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Trump votes early in Florida for US midterm elections
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Saturday voted early in his home state of Florida for the November 3 midterm elections, in which his Republican Party is battling to maintain control of Congress. Trump and his wife, Melania, cast their ballots ahead of an appearance by the president at a campaign rally in the southern US state of Georgia. Trump said he voted party line, or exclusively for members of his Republican Party. Asked by reporters after voting about corruption as a major issue for voters, Trump insisted that it was happening in districts and cities controlled by Democrats. “You ought to look at the real corruption — it’s Democrat corruption,” he said. The Republican billionaire, who has consistently refused to accept his defeat in the 2020 presidential election, baselessly alleging widespread voter fraud, reiterated allegations along those lines Saturday. “I ran and I won in 2016, and I won in 2020, too, but it didn’t work out that way,” he said at the Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections office in West Palm Beach. “It was a rigged election, but I won by millions of votes.” With 10 days to go until the midterms, which traditionally favor the party outside the White House, Trump faces dismal polls suggesting the Republicans will lose control of the House of Representatives and possibly the Senate. Without a Republican majority in Congress, the 80-year-old president would have little room to push through his legislative agenda during his final two years in office. He or his staff could also face numerous congressional investigations by Democrats, who have said they want to examine business dealings conducted by the president and those close to him through the family’s holding company since his return to the White House. AFP The post Trump votes early in Florida for US midterm elections appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Clashes break out in Paris, other French cities amid fresh protests
item.description: Clashes broke out Saturday in Paris and other French cities amid demonstrations held a week after others that degenerated into street violence and prompted a robust security backlash as President Emmanuel Macron seeks to restore order. Police arrested nearly 1,000 people as officers were confronted with “an extremely elevated level of violence” from black-clad “ultra-left” extremists, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said. Riot police squads fired tear gas at protesters in the capital as well as in Marseille, Lyon, Bordeaux, Lille, Toulouse, Montpellier and Nantes. Two people were “seriously” injured, Nunez said: one man in Toulouse, who reportedly had fingers blown off, and another person in Clermont-Ferrand. He did not give details of either case. Authorities had deployed 70,000 security forces across the country for the new marches, called to protest the cost of living. The violence came a week after rioting that saw public buildings vandalised, hundreds of shops looted and 2,700 people arrested, casting a pall over a country that goes to the polls in six months to choose a successor to Macron after 10 years. Nunez said Saturday’s outcome was more “positive” than a week ago, with more police on the streets acting more rapidly, conducting more pre-demonstration checks and better protecting businesses. There was nevertheless widespread anger at the government over a protest crackdown viewed as an assault on the right to protest. – Police battle ‘rioters’ – Saturday’s demonstrations drew between 410,000 and 800,000 people across the country, according to different estimates by authorities and the organising CGT union. The main Paris march had between 110,000 and 250,000 attendees, according to those sources. Macron’s government has ordered police to prevent protesters reaching city centres, where shops are concentrated, and in Paris and some other cities, partial curfews were imposed in certain urban zones. The French president had ordered non-union demonstrations be banned as “illegitimate”. In Paris, where many shops had boarded up windows to prevent looting, and the Louvre and the Musee d’Orsay museums shut for the day, the main demonstration passed off largely peacefully. The march had been pushed to the capital’s southeast rim under a last-minute order by authorities. Afterwards, though, clashes broke out as the crowd was dispersing. Nunez said the confrontations lasted two hours and involved “500 rioters” at the back of the march. AFP journalists saw police charge several times and vigorously use tear gas and batons against some, mostly young, protesters. “The police started moving towards everyone, telling them to get down and back off. They were just taking people down, you know, beating protesters,” one demonstrator bleeding from a baton blow to his face, who gave his first name as David, told AFP. – Ultra-right vs ultra-left – In the western city of Nantes, thousands of protesters broke through lines of police firing tear gas and a water
item.dc:creator: Ayobami
item.content:encoded: Clashes broke out Saturday in Paris and other French cities amid demonstrations held a week after others that degenerated into street violence and prompted a robust security backlash as President Emmanuel Macron seeks to restore order. Police arrested nearly 1,000 people as officers were confronted with “an extremely elevated level of violence” from black-clad “ultra-left” extremists, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said. Riot police squads fired tear gas at protesters in the capital as well as in Marseille, Lyon, Bordeaux, Lille, Toulouse, Montpellier and Nantes. Two people were “seriously” injured, Nunez said: one man in Toulouse, who reportedly had fingers blown off, and another person in Clermont-Ferrand. He did not give details of either case. Authorities had deployed 70,000 security forces across the country for the new marches, called to protest the cost of living. The violence came a week after rioting that saw public buildings vandalised, hundreds of shops looted and 2,700 people arrested, casting a pall over a country that goes to the polls in six months to choose a successor to Macron after 10 years. Nunez said Saturday’s outcome was more “positive” than a week ago, with more police on the streets acting more rapidly, conducting more pre-demonstration checks and better protecting businesses. There was nevertheless widespread anger at the government over a protest crackdown viewed as an assault on the right to protest. – Police battle ‘rioters’ – Saturday’s demonstrations drew between 410,000 and 800,000 people across the country, according to different estimates by authorities and the organising CGT union. The main Paris march had between 110,000 and 250,000 attendees, according to those sources. Macron’s government has ordered police to prevent protesters reaching city centres, where shops are concentrated, and in Paris and some other cities, partial curfews were imposed in certain urban zones. The French president had ordered non-union demonstrations be banned as “illegitimate”. In Paris, where many shops had boarded up windows to prevent looting, and the Louvre and the Musee d’Orsay museums shut for the day, the main demonstration passed off largely peacefully. The march had been pushed to the capital’s southeast rim under a last-minute order by authorities. Afterwards, though, clashes broke out as the crowd was dispersing. Nunez said the confrontations lasted two hours and involved “500 rioters” at the back of the march. AFP journalists saw police charge several times and vigorously use tear gas and batons against some, mostly young, protesters. “The police started moving towards everyone, telling them to get down and back off. They were just taking people down, you know, beating protesters,” one demonstrator bleeding from a baton blow to his face, who gave his first name as David, told AFP. – Ultra-right vs ultra-left – In the western city of Nantes, thousands of protesters broke through lines of police firing tear gas and a water cannon to reach the city centre, an AFP journalist there witnessed. Emma, 23, marching in the northwest city of Rennes, said she was angry at “everything happening at the moment”, denouncing the bans on demonstrations and the “repression” of the high schools student protests. Marching in the rain at the head of the protest in the northern city of Lille, 47-year-old Delphine insisted: “Neither the president, nor the weather will stop me from demonstrating.” In Lyon, police used tear gas to disperse around 1,000 people gathered in the south of the city. “If they prohibit protests then that means we are heading more and more towards a regime that is fascist, that is dictatorial,” said one 20-year-old protester in Lyon, who gave only his first name, Silem. In the southern cities of Cannes and Montpellier, far-right activists came out onto the streets seeking confrontations with “ultra-left militants”, in what authorities said was an unprecedented development. There was looting on the sidelines of the marches in Marseille and Grenoble, said police. Meanwhile, the Yellow Vests, who staged disruptive protests against Macron eight years ago, called for more demonstrations on October 31 for “the freedom to protest”. Far-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon, who marched in the Paris rally, said Macron “is going to understand that this is going to repeat itself every week”. – Protest against Le Pen’s party – Tensions were heightened by a rally in the city of Orleans by far-right leader Marine Le Pen’s National Rally party to kick off her campaign for the presidential election. Thousands of counter-protesters chanting anti-fascist slogans marched in the city. Police put their number at 13,000 while organisers said twice as many participated. The unrest across France highlighted the febrile political atmosphere ahead of the vote, in which Le Pen leads in surveys. Inflation in France, particularly affecting the cost of fuel, has surged since the start of the Middle East war in February. Protests have also been taking place in Italy, Belgium, Spain and Portugal over different issues, yet with some overlap on inflation and education problems. Italy has mobilised 500 troops to Milan after street violence there. The post Clashes break out in Paris, other French cities amid fresh protests appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ronaldinho returns to football with Italian third tier
item.description: Brazil legend Ronaldinho will make his playing return aged 46 next month for Ravenna, the third-division Italian club announced on Saturday. The 2002 World Cup winner’s move to Ravenna was announced in June. He is aiming to score his 300th career goal. The former Paris Saint-Germain, Barcelona and AC Milan playmaker retired in 2015, 10 years on from claiming the Ballon d’Or and has become a shareholder in Ravenna, situated between Venice and San Marino. “The wait now has a date: Sunday, November 15,” Ravenna said in a statement. “The Brazilian legend will wear the Ravenna FC shirt in the derby against Forli. “An event that will turn the eyes of the world toward the Bruno Benelli Stadium.” Ravenna are second in Group B of the Italian third tier, six points below leaders Spezia and are aiming for a return to Serie B for the first time since 2008. Vanguard News The post Ronaldinho returns to football with Italian third tier appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Southampton end West Ham’s unbeaten run, Burnley sack manager
item.description: Southampton ended West Ham’s nine-match unbeaten run with a 3-2 win at the London Stadium to surge into the Championship top six despite starting the season with a four-point deduction. Saints began the campaign with the points penalty after spying on opposition training sessions, which also cost them the chance of promotion in the play-off final last season. Kuryu Matsuki, James Bree and Lewis Dobbin all struck before half-time for the visitors, who are now within three points of the automatic promotion places. Kyle Walker-Peters and Tomas Soucek replied for the Hammers, but there were swathes of empty seats and boos by full-time as they missed the chance to go top. “This is a tough place to come, against a quality team, and we knew we needed to start strongly, so we worked on that all week,” said Saints boss Tonda Eckert after his side went 2-0 up inside the opening 10 minutes. “They made it tough for us in the second half, so it was important that we stayed brave to bring the result over the line.” Burnley sacked manager Nicky Hayen after just 14 games in charge following his side’s 4-1 defeat at Lincoln, which left the Clarets in the relegation zone. Relegated from the Premier League last season, former Club Brugge boss Hayen won just one of his 12 league matches in charge. “Burnley Football Club has dismissed head coach Nicky Hayen with immediate effect,” the club said in just a two-sentence statement. “The board has taken the decision following a disappointing start to the Championship season.” Swansea’s missed the chance to retake top spot after they were thrashed 5-0 by QPR at Loftus Road. Richard Kone scored a hat-trick inside the first 15 minutes before Jimmy Dunne’s double rounded off a remarkable scoreline that nudges Rangers into the play-off places. Adam Armstrong scored the only goal as fourth-placed Wolves beat struggling Watford 1-0 to move within two points of the automatic promotion places. AFP The post Southampton end West Ham’s unbeaten run, Burnley sack manager appeared first on Vanguard News .

Kyle Walker-Peters and Tomas Soucek replied for the Hammers, but there were swathes of empty seats and boos by full-time as they missed the chance to go top. “This is a tough place to come, against a quality team, and we knew we needed to start strongly, so we worked on that all week,” said Saints boss Tonda Eckert after his side went 2-0 up inside the opening 10 minutes. “They made it tough for us in the second half, so it was important that we stayed brave to bring the result over the line.” Burnley sacked manager Nicky Hayen after just 14 games in charge following his side’s 4-1 defeat at Lincoln, which left the Clarets in the relegation zone. Relegated from the Premier League last season, former Club Brugge boss Hayen won just one of his 12 league matches in charge. “Burnley Football Club has dismissed head coach Nicky Hayen with immediate effect,” the club said in just a two-sentence statement. “The board has taken the decision following a disappointing start to the Championship season.” Swansea’s missed the chance to retake top spot after they were thrashed 5-0 by QPR at Loftus Road. Richard Kone scored a hat-trick inside the first 15 minutes before Jimmy Dunne’s double rounded off a remarkable scoreline that nudges Rangers into the play-off places. Adam Armstrong scored the only goal as fourth-placed Wolves beat struggling Watford 1-0 to move within two points of the automatic promotion places. AFP The post Southampton end West Ham’s unbeaten run, Burnley sack manager appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: VIDEO: ‘Tinubu Fought For You’, Shettima Seeks North’s Support For Tinubu’s Re-Election
item.description: Vice President Kashim Shettima has appealed to voters in northern Nigeria to back President Bola Tinubu for a second term in 2027, arguing that the President has earned the region’s support through his past backing of northern political leaders. Shettima made the appeal on Saturday at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign flag-off in Kaduna, where he urged voters to support the party’s candidates across all levels of government. “We have come to ask you to renew a second time for the APC from top to bottom,” he said. The Vice President cited Tinubu’s support for northern figures, including former President Muhammadu Buhari, as a reason for voters in the region to reciprocate by supporting his re-election bid. item.title: Spurs Seal Rare Win At Chelsea As Palmer Sees Red
item.description: Tottenham clinched a Premier League win at Chelsea for just the second time in 36 years as a woeful own goal from Blues keeper Mike Penders was followed by Cole Palmer’s red card in Saturday’s 2-0 victory. Roberto De Zerbi’s side clinched their second successive league win thanks to Penders’s howler in the second half at a rain-lashed Stamford Bridge. Chelsea forward Palmer was sent off for a second booking moments later before Mathys Tel produced a superb solo effort to condemn the Blues to their first home defeat against Tottenham since 2018. Since 1990, Tottenham had won just once in 41 previous away matches against London rivals Chelsea in all competitions. Ending that miserable run gave Tottenham only their second win in their last 16 league games against Chelsea, both home and away, and their first since 2023. English referee Chris Kavanagh shows a red card to Chelsea’s English midfielder #10 Cole Palmer (R) during the English Premier League football match between Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge in London on October 24, 2026. (Photo by Glyn KIRK / AFP) After a dismal start to the season, Tottenham have climbed to 12th place after building on Monday’s win against Coventry, which ended their wait for a first league win this season. It was a bitter blow for fourth-placed Chelsea, who had beaten Bournemouth and Everton in their previous two league games. They were booed off at full-time and remain very much a work in progress under Xabi Alonso in the Spaniard’s first season in charge. With Joao Pedro sidelined by a late injury, Morgan Rogers was Chelsea’s central striker, but their revamped attack was short of bite. Teed up by Rogers after Pedro Neto stole possession from Mateus Fernandes, Palmer went close to an early opener with a curler that Antonin Kinsky tipped over at full stretch. Tottenham responded with a spell of probing pressure as Omar Marmoush met Andy Robertson’s cross with a shot that was repelled by Penders. Alonso’s men pieced together the best move of the half with a flurry of one-touch passes to reach Jordan Henderson on the edge of the area, but the midfielder’s low drive was palmed away by Kinsky. Tottenham Hotspur’s Egyptian midfielder #22 Omar Marmoush (C) vies with Chelsea’s Ecuadorian midfielder #25 Moises Caicedo (L) and Chelsea’s French defender #05 Maxence Lacroix (R) during the English Premier League football match between Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge in London on October 24, 2026. (Photo by Glyn KIRK / AFP) Spurs spring a surprise Neto tested Kinsky with a fierce blast but the Tottenham keeper was up to the task with a save at his near post. item.dc:creator: Donatus Anichukwueze
item.content:encoded: Tottenham clinched a Premier League win at Chelsea for just the second time in 36 years as a woeful own goal from Blues keeper Mike Penders was followed by Cole Palmer’s red card in Saturday’s 2-0 victory. Roberto De Zerbi’s side clinched their second successive league win thanks to Penders’s howler in the second half at a rain-lashed Stamford Bridge. Chelsea forward Palmer was sent off for a second booking moments later before Mathys Tel produced a superb solo effort to condemn the Blues to their first home defeat against Tottenham since 2018. Since 1990, Tottenham had won just once in 41 previous away matches against London rivals Chelsea in all competitions. Ending that miserable run gave Tottenham only their second win in their last 16 league games against Chelsea, both home and away, and their first since 2023. English referee Chris Kavanagh shows a red card to Chelsea’s English midfielder #10 Cole Palmer (R) during the English Premier League football match between Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge in London on October 24, 2026. (Photo by Glyn KIRK / AFP) After a dismal start to the season, Tottenham have climbed to 12th place after building on Monday’s win against Coventry, which ended their wait for a first league win this season. It was a bitter blow for fourth-placed Chelsea, who had beaten Bournemouth and Everton in their previous two league games. They were booed off at full-time and remain very much a work in progress under Xabi Alonso in the Spaniard’s first season in charge. With Joao Pedro sidelined by a late injury, Morgan Rogers was Chelsea’s central striker, but their revamped attack was short of bite. Teed up by Rogers after Pedro Neto stole possession from Mateus Fernandes, Palmer went close to an early opener with a curler that Antonin Kinsky tipped over at full stretch. Tottenham responded with a spell of probing pressure as Omar Marmoush met Andy Robertson’s cross with a shot that was repelled by Penders. Alonso’s men pieced together the best move of the half with a flurry of one-touch passes to reach Jordan Henderson on the edge of the area, but the midfielder’s low drive was palmed away by Kinsky. Tottenham Hotspur’s Egyptian midfielder #22 Omar Marmoush (C) vies with Chelsea’s Ecuadorian midfielder #25 Moises Caicedo (L) and Chelsea’s French defender #05 Maxence Lacroix (R) during the English Premier League football match between Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge in London on October 24, 2026. (Photo by Glyn KIRK / AFP) Spurs spring a surprise Neto tested Kinsky with a fierce blast but the Tottenham keeper was up to the task with a save at his near post. Tottenham suffered a blow when often-injured midfielder James Maddison limped off in a premature end to only his second start since May 2025. Maddison had already missed training sessions since his long-awaited start against Coventry and his latest fitness setback suggested it was a failed gamble to start him at the Bridge. In keeping with the sloppy fare, Neto fired straight at Kinsky from a dangerous position after Palmer pounced on Sandro Tonali’s wayward pass. When Palmer’s run was halted by Fernandes’s handball, the Chelsea star escaped with a yellow card after barging into his rival with such aggression that the Tottenham midfielder was sent crashing to the sodden turf. Tottenham exacted swift revenge in the 77th minute. Fernandes’s in-swinging corner should have been caught by Penders, but he opted for a punch that was completely mistimed as he diverted the ball into his net for a comical own goal. It was a horrible moment for the 21-year-old Penders, who was making his first league start in the absence of Emiliano Martinez following jaw surgery. Rubbing salt into Chelsea’s wounds, Palmer was dismissed three minutes later for an ugly stamp on Conor Gallagher. Tel wrapped up Tottenham’s memorable triumph in fitting style in the 87th minute, skipping away from Chelsea’s flat-footed defence to drill a fine finish into the bottom corner from the edge of the area. item.title: Why Stanley Matthews’ Ballon d’Or triumph echoes down the years for Harry Kane | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: In 1956, the Blackpool great was recognised for his force of individual will, the very thing that makes the Bayern and England striker the standout candiate Systems football began In 1963 (On the hallowed turf at Wembley) With the impact of a cynical foul By Gino Pivatelli. At that moment in the European Cup final, when the hard-working Milan forward, brought in to combat Benfica’s Mário Coluna, caught the great playmaker, football of the individual came to an end. The foul not only checked a promising break, but broke a bone in Coluna’s foot. Without substitutes, he hobbled on, diminished, and Milan won 2-1 to lift the trophy and register the first victory for a team that prioritised the system over the individual. Modern football was born. Continue reading...

item.description: Athletes’ scramble to control – and monetise – their digital identities at the cutting edge of AI rights deals Get our new political email , free app or daily news podcast The Socceroos star stares at the camera as he strides through an enormous atrium, the sound of his football boots on polished concrete echoing around him. Suddenly, he spawns four digital clones that peel off out of view to re-emerge in different settings around the world. This scene from a social media video is fake and generated by artificial intelligence. But it has been authorised by the very real 22-year-old footballer, Cristian Volpato, the latest professional athlete to licence and monetise his AI likeness. Continue reading...

item.title: Pennsylvania will require labels on AI-generated ads
item.description: On Thursday, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro signed the Artificial Intelligence Deceptive Advertising Act into law, requiring disclosures on AI-generated ads. The law requires any ad - whether it's a still image, video, audio, or text - that "has been significantly modified or generated by artificial intelligence" to include a label in the same format as the ad itself. That applies to TV commercials from multi-billion-dollar companies , as well as restaurants' ugly, crowded flyers about their wing specials. Pennsylvania is one of the first states to require disclosures on AI content. And it requires those labels regardless of where an ad … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Zlatan Ibile & Davita Omoniyi Celebrate Yoruba Heritage in Lemon Yellow and Mint Green
item.description: Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi celebrating their Yoruba cultural heritage during their wedding ceremony. Lemon yellow and mint green? Now that’s a colour combination we can get behind. For their second traditional wedding look, Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi ( Omoniyi Temidayo Raphael ) have switched things up, trading their earlier burgundy and ivory outfits for a softer palette that feels right at home at a Yoruba wedding. And if you thought one outfit change was enough for this celebration, you know Nigerian weddings better than that! Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi in custom Mazelle Bridal pastel Yoruba traditional attire, styled by Goodnews Emmanuel Icon. After honouring Davita’s Edo heritage in their first look, the couple are now celebrating Zlatan’s Yoruba roots in coordinated outfits by Mazelle Bridal. Davita wears a custom lemon-yellow gown with a sculpted, corset-style bodice, a sweetheart-inspired neckline and long sleeves with flared cuffs. Mint-green appliqué forms swirling, floral-inspired patterns across the bodice and fitted, floor-length skirt, with gold-toned accents adding extra detail. Davita Omoniyi showcasing her custom Mazelle Bridal outfit for her Yoruba traditional wedding look. She completes the look with a large, pleated lemon-yellow gele and matching sheer fabric draped over her arm. A green statement necklace, matching earrings and a mint-green clutch bring the accessories together, while the soft yellow and green palette gives her bridal look a fresh, coordinated finish. Davita Omoniyi wearing a pleated circular gele and sheer veil for her second traditional wedding outfit change. Zlatan matches her in a custom mint-green agbada by Mazelle Bridal, featuring subtle embroidery across the chest. He finishes his outfit with a structured fila, layers of white beads and a carved green walking stick that picks up the colour of his attire. Zlatan Ibile in a custom Mazelle Bridal Agbada set for his Yoruba traditional wedding. Styled by Goodnews Emmanuel Icon, the couple pose hand in hand against a plum backdrop. Their first look celebrated Davita’s Edo heritage, and this second outfit honours Zlatan’s Yoruba roots, giving their wedding wardrobe two lovely cultural chapters. And with lemon yellow and mint green taking centre stage, this outfit change has given us another reason to keep up with their wedding style. Davita Omoniyi and Zlatan Ibile posing together in matching pastel Mazelle Bridal attire. *** Photo Credit: Zlatan Ibile/Instagram The post Zlatan Ibile & Davita Omoniyi Celebrate Yoruba Heritage in Lemon Yellow and Mint Green appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.description: Hammers humbled at home; Swansea thrashed 5-0 Burnley sack manager Hayen after 4-1 loss at Lincoln Southampton announced themselves in the promotion race with a statement 3-2 win at the pre-season title favourites, West Ham . Kuryu Matsuki, James Bree and Lewis Dobbin were all on target in a chaotic first half, while Kyle Walker-Peters and Tomas Soucek replied for the Hammers. Nuno Espírito Santo’s side would have gone top with a win but instead saw their nine-match unbeaten run halted. There were thousands of empty seats by the end at the London Stadium, with those who stayed booing the Hammers off. Southampton, deducted four points at the start of the season, are now just two points behind West Ham. Continue reading...

item.title: France: Clashes erupt as protests sweep across cities
item.description: 🇫🇷 The Ministry of the Interior estimates at least 410,000 people rallied across France for Saturday’s protests against the high cost of living, including 110,000 in Paris. The situation in Paris remained largely "calm" during the day, while clashes broke out in other cities following attempts to enter unauthorised areas.

item.title: Italy hit by new cost of living protests
item.description: Soldiers were deployed across Milan and luxury boutiques boarded up as protesters took to the streets again on Saturday, a week after looting and clashes with police. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni announced a series of measures, including sending an additional 500 soldiers to the city and introducing tougher penalties for minors, who police said made up a large proportion of last week’s violent protesters. Surveillance helicopters circled central Piazza del Duomo, while soldiers patrolled in groups alongside military vehicles and a water cannon. Some visitors said they would leave the city centre if violence broke out again. Our Rome correspondent, Seema Gupta, has the latest.

item.title: France: Protests continue while police fire tear gas at demonstrators
item.description: A total of 410,000 people took part in demonstrations across France on Saturday – including 110,000 in Paris – as part of a day of rallies focussed on purchasing power and the defence of public services, the Interior Ministry told AFP. The turnout was slightly lower than last week, which saw 550,000 people take to the streets. Meanwhile, according to the union responsible for organising the authorised events, 800,000 people participated in the demonstrations nationwide on Saturday, with 250,000 in the capital. Clashes broke out in several cities, including Paris, Lyon, Rennes, Nantes, Bordeaux, Nice, and Marseille. Matthew Mary-Caruchet shares further details.

item.title: Arsenal Beat Everton To Join Man City At Premier League Summit
item.description: Arsenal beat Everton 2-0 on Saturday to pull level with Manchester City at the top of the Premier League, rediscovering their taste for set-piece goals at a rainswept Emirates. Ezri Konsa bundled the ball into the net in the opening minutes for his first goal for the club since joining from Aston Villa in August. Fellow centre-back Gabriel Magalhaes doubled the home side’s lead midway through the second period. The win meant Arsenal took full advantage of City’s 2-1 defeat at Villa Park in Saturday’s kick-off — the first time Enzo Maresca’s men had dropped points this season. Both teams are now on 21 points, but City, the Gunners’ main title rivals in recent seasons, have a superior goal difference. Arsenal’s Brazilian defender #06 Gabriel Magalhaes (R) heads home their second goal during the English Premier League football match between Arsenal and Everton at the Emirates Stadium in London on October 24, 2026. (Photo by Henry Nicholls / AFP) Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta was forced to shuffle his pack after Bukayo Saka suffered a muscle injury in the midweek Champions League draw at Bayern Munich, picking Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze as his wide players. Arteta was already short of wingers, with Christos Tzolis still sidelined and both Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard sold during the summer transfer window. The home team started strongly and took the lead in the seventh minute after their third corner, following a scramble in the box. Martin Odegaard’s inswinging delivery was flicked on by Gabriel. Everton goalkeeper Jordan Pickford got his fingertips to the bouncing ball but it fell to Konsa, who poked it home at the back post. Set-piece kings It was the first non-penalty set-piece goal in all competitions in the current campaign for Arsenal — who earned a reputation last season as set-piece kings as they won their first Premier League title in a generation. Everton responded positively. Tyrique George’s shot was deflected behind by Ben White but Arsenal were largely in control. Madueke, recently deemed surplus to requirements by the watching England boss Thomas Tuchel, impressed on the right wing, spinning and hitting the side netting on the half-hour mark. Arsenal’s English midfielder #20 Noni Madueke crosses the ball during the English Premier League football match between Arsenal and Everton at the Emirates Stadium in London on October 24, 2026. (Photo by Henry Nicholls / AFP) Arsenal had a major scare as the clock ticked towards half-time when a careless header from Ben White back to his goalkeeper David Raya was intercepted by Thierno Barry, but the Everton forward was unable to make clean contact and Raya made the save. Gunners midfielder Mikel Merino flashed a header over the bar in the closing moments of the half, which ended with 13 shots and 10 corners for the home side, but just the solitary goal. Ezri Konsa bundled the ball into the net in the opening minutes for his first goal for the club since joining from Aston Villa in August. Fellow centre-back Gabriel Magalhaes doubled the home side’s lead midway through the second period. Both teams are now on 21 points, but City, the Gunners’ main title rivals in recent seasons, have a superior goal difference. Arsenal’s Brazilian defender #06 Gabriel Magalhaes (R) heads home their second goal during the English Premier League football match between Arsenal and Everton at the Emirates Stadium in London on October 24, 2026. (Photo by Henry Nicholls / AFP) Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta was forced to shuffle his pack after Bukayo Saka suffered a muscle injury in the midweek Champions League draw at Bayern Munich, picking Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze as his wide players. Arteta was already short of wingers, with Christos Tzolis still sidelined and both Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard sold during the summer transfer window. The home team started strongly and took the lead in the seventh minute after their third corner, following a scramble in the box. Martin Odegaard’s inswinging delivery was flicked on by Gabriel. Everton goalkeeper Jordan Pickford got his fingertips to the bouncing ball but it fell to Konsa, who poked it home at the back post. Set-piece kings It was the first non-penalty set-piece goal in all competitions in the current campaign for Arsenal — who earned a reputation last season as set-piece kings as they won their first Premier League title in a generation. Everton responded positively. Tyrique George’s shot was deflected behind by Ben White but Arsenal were largely in control. Madueke, recently deemed surplus to requirements by the watching England boss Thomas Tuchel, impressed on the right wing, spinning and hitting the side netting on the half-hour mark. Arsenal’s English midfielder #20 Noni Madueke crosses the ball during the English Premier League football match between Arsenal and Everton at the Emirates Stadium in London on October 24, 2026. (Photo by Henry Nicholls / AFP) Arsenal had a major scare as the clock ticked towards half-time when a careless header from Ben White back to his goalkeeper David Raya was intercepted by Thierno Barry, but the Everton forward was unable to make clean contact and Raya made the save. Gunners midfielder Mikel Merino flashed a header over the bar in the closing moments of the half, which ended with 13 shots and 10 corners for the home side, but just the solitary goal. Gabriel went down in pain 10 minutes after the restart, stretching to intercept the ball, but was able to resume after treatment on the pitch. Arteta made a triple substitution in the 68th minute, bringing on Kai Havertz, Bruno Guimaraes and Riccardo Calafiori. Moments later they were 2-0 ahead when Gabriel rose to head home White’s cross after a neatly worked move down the right. Teenager Max Dowman, who became the youngest-ever Premier League goalscorer in the same fixture last season, was introduced for the final 10 minutes. Everton almost pulled a goal back when Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall flashed a header just wide of Raya’s post but that was the last major scare on a satisfactory day for Arsenal. item.title: How AI Can Expand Opportunities for African Youth – Discussions to Expect at Goalkeepers 2026 Dakar
item.description: AI could be a great equaliser, but only if it’s built intentionally to benefit the people who need it most. Credit: Gates Foundation . During the 2026 ADF-YGL Convening in Lagos , young leaders from across the world, including Africa, gathered at Learn2Earn Academy, an AI talent factory founded by Iyinoluwa Aboyeji . There, the global leaders were introduced to a few students who have been using AI to build solutions for some of the day-to-day challenges that Africans, Nigerians specifically, face. One of them was Anas Masama, who showcased ‘Morrow’, a fintech app that allows offline transfers without internet connectivity. Anas explained that despite the wide coverage of internet providers in Nigeria, the internet’s strength fluctuates or sometimes goes offline and leaves Nigerians stranded at a point of payment. With AI, he built ‘Morrow’ to solve two problems: 1) The embarrassment that a Nigerian might feel due to bad internet connectivity. 2) Time. Anas’ invention is an example of the potential opportunities that exist when Africans leverage AI to solve basic issues. While there are concerns about the risks of AI use in Africa, including hallucinations, stereotypical results and many others, it remains one of the fastest-growing technological advancements in recent times. AI continues to grow and become more efficient, and the most urgent task Africans can embark on is to upskill in how to adopt AI for better use, so the continent doesn’t get left behind. In the 2026 Goalkeepers Report , Bill Gates calls for three actions now that will help AI improve lives and livelihoods for more people in the years ahead: Make AI tools work in every language people speak; ground AI tools in local data; and invest in people and access in the places and populations they are intended to serve. All three suggestions apply to Africa so it can properly leverage AI to expand opportunities. At present, despite how expansive AI has become, it is built in places far away from Africa. This is why Africans, who have access to local data and speak African languages, should build AI tools that incorporate local data and African languages for better use. This way, AI has access to specific data of Africans and will allow it to better understand cultural contexts and pragmatics. This will make a great equaliser rather than make things less equal. Of course, Africans still encounter basic challenges like electricity, connectivity, access to phones, and other issues, but those who have access must maximise it greatly to help others. This year’s Goalkeepers 2026 is centred around this conversation. After hosting engaging and immersive events in the Nordics and New York, Goalkeepers is coming to Dakar on October 29. This event, “Equitable AI and the Future of African Youth”, aims to discuss how AI can create opportunities for Africans across various sectors while also addressing the challenges the continent faces. What are some of the areas AI can expand opportunities for Afr
item.dc:creator: BellaNaija Features
item.content:encoded: AI could be a great equaliser, but only if it’s built intentionally to benefit the people who need it most. Credit: Gates Foundation . During the 2026 ADF-YGL Convening in Lagos , young leaders from across the world, including Africa, gathered at Learn2Earn Academy, an AI talent factory founded by Iyinoluwa Aboyeji . There, the global leaders were introduced to a few students who have been using AI to build solutions for some of the day-to-day challenges that Africans, Nigerians specifically, face. One of them was Anas Masama, who showcased ‘Morrow’, a fintech app that allows offline transfers without internet connectivity. Anas explained that despite the wide coverage of internet providers in Nigeria, the internet’s strength fluctuates or sometimes goes offline and leaves Nigerians stranded at a point of payment. With AI, he built ‘Morrow’ to solve two problems: 1) The embarrassment that a Nigerian might feel due to bad internet connectivity. 2) Time. Anas’ invention is an example of the potential opportunities that exist when Africans leverage AI to solve basic issues. While there are concerns about the risks of AI use in Africa, including hallucinations, stereotypical results and many others, it remains one of the fastest-growing technological advancements in recent times. AI continues to grow and become more efficient, and the most urgent task Africans can embark on is to upskill in how to adopt AI for better use, so the continent doesn’t get left behind. In the 2026 Goalkeepers Report , Bill Gates calls for three actions now that will help AI improve lives and livelihoods for more people in the years ahead: Make AI tools work in every language people speak; ground AI tools in local data; and invest in people and access in the places and populations they are intended to serve. All three suggestions apply to Africa so it can properly leverage AI to expand opportunities. At present, despite how expansive AI has become, it is built in places far away from Africa. This is why Africans, who have access to local data and speak African languages, should build AI tools that incorporate local data and African languages for better use. This way, AI has access to specific data of Africans and will allow it to better understand cultural contexts and pragmatics. This will make a great equaliser rather than make things less equal. Of course, Africans still encounter basic challenges like electricity, connectivity, access to phones, and other issues, but those who have access must maximise it greatly to help others. This year’s Goalkeepers 2026 is centred around this conversation. After hosting engaging and immersive events in the Nordics and New York, Goalkeepers is coming to Dakar on October 29. This event, “Equitable AI and the Future of African Youth”, aims to discuss how AI can create opportunities for Africans across various sectors while also addressing the challenges the continent faces. What are some of the areas AI can expand opportunities for African youth? Education Access to quality education remains one of the core issues facing sub-Saharan Africa. With AI, African youth can gain access to quality education, regardless of where they live. Students can use AI-powered tutors to explain difficult subjects, practise questions, learn new languages and receive feedback based on their performance. Teachers can also use AI to prepare lesson plans and develop learning materials for students with different abilities. Developed countries like the Netherlands use AI-powered platforms such as Snappet to analyse students’ work and provide exercises suited to their learning levels. UNESCO has also highlighted Rori , an AI tutor that reaches students in Sierra Leone and Ghana through WhatsApp. These examples show how African innovators can develop educational tools that work on mobile phones, use local languages and require less internet data. For young Africans, this also creates opportunities to build educational technology companies, develop learning applications and provide digital tutoring services to students locally and abroad. Perhaps, instead of travelling thousands of miles to gain degrees from top universities in the world, AI can help bring education to doorsteps in Africa. Finance and Investment Financial literacy is one of the major conversations in the modern world. A while back, Fu’ad Lawal shared on X (formerly Twitter) that he asked ChatGPT to pick three stocks in June last year. He wrote in the tweet, “It recommended three companies he knew next to nothing about at the time. Today, they’re up over 200% cumulatively.” This is how AI can help people understand financial information and make more informed decisions African youth can develop financial tools that help people with irregular incomes manage their money, compare savings products and understand investment opportunities. AI can also help small businesses prepare financial records that make it easier to apply for loans. Although, AI cannot reliably predict every market movement or guarantee investment returns. Its recommendations can be inaccurate or biased, so users must verify information and consider their financial circumstances before investing. Agriculture Agriculture remains an important source of livelihood across Africa, but farmers face challenges such as unpredictable weather, pests, poor soil conditions and difficulties accessing markets. AI can help farmers make better decisions by analysing weather forecasts, satellite images, soil conditions and crop diseases. Africans can create affordable farming applications that send weather alerts, identify crop diseases and connect farmers to buyers. Tools that work through SMS, WhatsApp or offline mobile applications could also help farmers who have limited internet access. These solutions can create opportunities for young people in agritech, agricultural research and food distribution. It even extends to the chain of food distribution. Other areas of opportunity include employment and skills development. Today, anyone can get into tech and vibe code. Of course, they still need to be taught, but that beginner’s gap has been closed. Despite these opportunities, the challenges of inaccurate information, bias, privacy concerns, and the possibility that automation could displace some jobs remain a significant concern. Also, limited electricity, expensive internet access and inadequate digital infrastructure may also prevent many African youths from benefiting. This is why it is important for governments, educational institutions, businesses and technology companies to invest in digital infrastructure, affordable access and AI training. A 2025 study projected that AI could contribute between 0.4 and 1.3 percentage points to annual labour productivity growth over the next decade in highly exposed economies such as the United States and the United Kingdom, depending on adoption and other assumptions. While these projections do not guarantee similar outcomes for Africa, they demonstrate why readiness and adoption matter, which is why Goalkeepers Dakar 2026 is momentous. As AI continues to rapidly develop and expand, African youth cannot afford to be left behind. The post How AI Can Expand Opportunities for African Youth – Discussions to Expect at Goalkeepers 2026 Dakar appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: ‘You Created Hunger And Poverty,’ Tinubu Tells Opposition At Kaduna Campaign Kick-Off
item.description: President Bola Tinubu on Saturday accused the opposition of creating hunger and poverty in Nigeria, pushing back against criticism of his administration’s handling of the economy as he launched his campaign for a second term in office. Speaking at the All Progressives Congress (APC) 2027 presidential campaign flag-off at the Kaduna Township Stadium, Tinubu said his government was working to eradicate the hardship blamed on the opposition. He also promised supporters prosperity if re-elected, assuring them that they would not regret giving him a second term. “You gave me joy to remember the victory you gave me to become president. I come again to thank you for that, to seek your mandate for the second term, to keep a promise on prosperity, continuity and progress. I have an argument, I hear my opponents talking about hunger and poverty. Who created it? They did! They created hunger, they created poverty, we are trying to eradicate it,” he said. “We pay salaries regularly, our governors are working, I am proud of them, they are developing. To you, the children of our country, it’s a promise of a second term – prosperity; you will not regret going to the votes.” ﻿ The removal of fuel subsidy has also emerged as a major issue ahead of the 2027 election, with some opposition figures, including former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, promising to restore it if elected. However, Tinubu defended the policy at the Kaduna rally, urging supporters to be wary of what he described as misleading claims by his opponents. “Be careful; watch them. Don’t let them lie to you. What is past is in the past. Fuel subsidy is in our past: no more corruption, no more falsification of invoices, no more lies, no more smuggling of fuel,” he said. Also speaking at the campaign flag-off, Vice President Kashim Shettima said Tinubu had consistently supported northern political leaders over the years. Shettima cited Tinubu’s backing of Atiku Abubakar in 2007, Nuhu Ribadu in 2011 and former President Muhammadu Buhari in the 2015 and 2019 elections. “President Bola Tinubu is one person who has fiercely identified with the north over the years. It is pertinent to mention that when former vice-president Atiku Abubakar was harassed and chased off the PDP with his tail between his legs, he ran to the lion of Bourdillon who gave him political succour, support and a platform to contest for the presidency of this country in 2007. In 2011, Asiwaju supported another northerner, Nuhu Ribadu, and in 2015 and 2019, he supported our late president Muhammadu Buhari,” Shettima said. The host governor, Uba Sani, also urged APC supporters to remain vigilant, alleging that opposition parties had expanded their campaign tactics from social media platforms to the use of artificial intelligence (AI). “The opposition have now upgraded their campaign from Facebook and Twitter to AI. I want to call the attention of our supporters to be very watchful, to be vigilant,” he said. Other party stalwarts at the ev

I want to call the attention of our supporters to be very watchful, to be vigilant,” he said. Other party stalwarts at the event included the Director-General of the campaign, Senator Abdulaziz Yari; Senate President Godswill Akpabio; Minister of Works Dave Umahi; First Lady Remi Tinubu; APC National Chairman Nentawe Yilwatda; and governors from the North-West, among others. Crowds of APC supporters, dressed in different uniforms and wearing customised hats while waving party flags, filled the stadium and cheered the speakers throughout the event. item.title: Scottish Premiership: Kelsy fires Rangers to emphatic win; Dundee United pip Aberdeen
item.description: Rangers 4-0 St Johnstone; Dundee United 3-2 Aberdeen Kevin Kelsy scores two to sink 10-man Saints Derek McInnes asked his Rangers side to be “brilliant” against St Johnstone and was rewarded with a 4-0 Premiership win at Ibrox. After dropping two points at Dundee last Saturday , the Light Blues dominated the first half but only led at the interval through a goal in the 29th minute from the Venezuela forward Kevin Kelsy. Saints started the second half brightly but goals from the Gers striker Ryan Naderi in the 61st minute and Kelsy again five minutes later had the home side cruising. The Saints substitute Kai Fotheringham was shown a straight red card by Chris Graham in the 74th minute for his high challenge on the midfielder Nico Raskin, before the substitute Tochi Chukwuani added a fourth for the hosts with three minutes remaining. This story will be updated after Sunday’s matches Continue reading...

item.title: Davido, Zlatan & Shoday Turn Their “Nakupenda” Performance Into a London Sing-Along
item.description: Shoday, Zlatan Ibile, and Davido performing Nakupenda live on stage during their London concert setup. Photo Credit: Davido/Instagram “Oh my God, what is this? (What is what?)” You already know what comes next. We’re taking you straight to London, where Davido , Zlatan and Shoday had an entire arena singing along to “ Nakupenda ”. And judging by the crowd, nobody needed convincing to join in. Phones were up, voices were loud, and thousands of fans were enjoying every moment of the performance. There’s something so lovely about watching a song travel from our speakers to a stage thousands of miles away, with a crowd singing every word right back to the artistes. That’s exactly what happened when Davido and Zlatan performed “Nakupenda” alongside Shoday, giving the London audience a performance filled with music, dancing and some very happy fans. Davido took to the stage in a white tank top and green trousers, moving across the platform as the audience sang along. Zlatan joined him in a tactical vest and red trousers, bringing his familiar dance moves into the mix. With dancers adding to the performance and the crowd responding to every verse, there was hardly a moment when the arena wasn’t buzzing. And can we talk about those phone flashlights? Seeing thousands of them raised across the arena while everyone sang together was such a beautiful sight. It’s one thing to enjoy “Nakupenda” through your headphones, but hearing an entire crowd sing it back to Davido, Zlatan and Shoday is a whole different experience. Watch Davido, Zlatan and Shoday perform “Nakupenda” live in London below. The post Davido, Zlatan & Shoday Turn Their “Nakupenda” Performance Into a London Sing-Along appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .
